target.title: fix(security): route temp workspaces through private OpenClaw temp root (#101224)
target.body:
Closes #101224

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where running `openclaw skills install` or `openclaw skills update` could change `/tmp` permissions from `0o1777` (sticky + world-writable) to `0o0700` (owner-only), breaking access to the shared system temp directory for other processes and services. Affects Linux hosts where `os.tmpdir()` resolves to `/tmp`.

The same bug affects ClawHub plugin (`openclaw plugins install clawhub:...`) and package archive downloads via the same code path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is that ClawHub skill and package download flows passed `os.tmpdir()` (`/tmp`) as the root directory to `@openclaw/fs-safe` temp workspaces, whose `ensurePrivateDirectory` helper calls `chmod(root, 0o700)` to enforce private permissions. When `root` is a shared OS directory like `/tmp`, this mutates system-level permissions.

The fix routes all temp workspace operations through `resolvePreferredOpenClawTmpDir()`, which returns the private `/tmp/openclaw` directory (or a user-scoped fallback `{os.tmpdir()}/openclaw-{uid}`). This directory is already owned by OpenClaw and has safe `0o700` permissions — changing its mode does not affect other system processes.

Six call sites were identified and unified: `withTempDir`'s default root in `install-source-utils.ts`, and 5 explicit `tmpDir: os.tmpdir()` overrides in `clawhub.ts` covering ClawHub skill archive downloads, skill archive URL downloads, GitHub source archive downloads, and package archive downloads (both archive and ClawPack artifact paths). No external API changes, no new dependencies.

## User Impact

ClawHub skill and plugin installation no longer risk corrupting `/tmp` permissions. All temporary workspace operations — ClawHub downloads, archive extraction staging, and git skill cloning — now consistently use the private OpenClaw temp root instead of raw `/tmp`. For most users this is invisible; for users running `auditd` or sharing a system with other services, `/tmp` sticky-bit and world-writable permissions are preserved.

## Evidence

- **Source-reproducible audit trail**: Issue reporter's `auditd` logs confirmed `chmod` syscalls on `/tmp` from the same process chain (`openclaw-skills`).
- **fs-safe source verification**: Published `@openclaw/fs-safe@0.4.1` `ensurePrivateDirectory` calls `fs.chmod(root, 0o700)` on the provided `rootDir`.
- **Focused regression coverage**: Added `install-source-utils.chmod.test.ts` that mocks an isolated parent temp root with `0o1777` permissions and verifies: (1) `withTempDir` uses the OpenClaw private temp root, and (2) the parent directory permissions remain unchanged (`0o1777`) after the temp workspace completes.

  ```
  ✓ |unit| src/skills/lifecycle/clawhub.test.ts (74 tests)
  ```
  
- **real behavior proof**
  ✓ PASS: /tmp permissions unchanged (1777) — temp workspace correctly isolated under /tmp/openclaw (700)

target.title: fix(agents): route streamProxy request through fetchWithSsrFGuard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `streamProxy` function in `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts:301` issues an outgoing POST to the operator-configured `${options.proxyUrl}/api/stream` endpoint via the un-guarded global `fetch`. From openclaw's perspective the proxy URL is operator-controlled but the response body is **not** trusted: a misconfigured or hostile proxyUrl (e.g. one whose DNS A record rebinds to a private/internal IP between the lookup and the connect, or which streams an unbounded response body) currently bypasses every SSRF and byte-cap protection owned by `fetchWithSsrFGuard`. The SSE-byte guards in `proxy.ts` only run *after* the request has already been issued and the response headers received, so they cannot defend against the request itself.

This PR wraps the outgoing fetch with `fetchWithSsrFGuard` in STRICT mode and locks the hostname to the operator-configured proxy URL via `policy.allowedHostnames`, so the same DNS-pin / private-network / body-cap / dispatcher seam used elsewhere in agents now applies to proxy egress. The existing `.catch(...).finally(...)` chain (timeout translation + requestAbort.clear) is preserved verbatim; the guard's `release` runs in the outer `finally` so the dispatcher and DNS-pin resources are reclaimed regardless of whether the stream terminates normally, hits an SSE-byte cap, or is aborted.

## Changes

- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts:13` — add `import { fetchWithSsrFGuard, GUARDED_FETCH_MODE } from "../../infra/net/fetch-guard.js"`.
- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts:289` — declare `let releaseGuarded: (() => Promise<void>) | undefined` in the IIFE scope so the outer `finally` can call it.
- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts:299-336` — replace `await fetch(...)` with `await fetchWithSsrFGuard({ url, init: { method, headers, body, signal }, mode: GUARDED_FETCH_MODE.STRICT, policy: { allowedHostnames: [new URL(options.proxyUrl).hostname] }, auditContext: "proxy-stream" })`. Catch/finally chain preserved. `response = guarded.response` and `releaseGuarded = guarded.release`.
- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.ts:431-436` — outer `finally` now also calls `await releaseGuarded?.()` inside its own `try/catch` so guard release failures cannot replace the primary result.
- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts:3` — add `createServer, type AddressInfo` import.
- `src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts:564-612` — inline test that drives the production `streamProxy` end-to-end against a real `node:http` loopback server (no `vi.stubGlobal("fetch")`), proving the guard's allowedHostnames policy accepts the operator host while DNS pin + dispatcher + post-stream release hold.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `streamProxy` now routes its POST to `${proxyUrl}/api/stream` through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with hostname locked to the operator-configured proxy URL; DNS rebinding, private-network target, body-byte-cap, and timeout protections now apply to proxy egress.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node 22.19, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts --run`
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```bash
  git checkout fix/proxy-stream-ssrf-guard
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/runtime/proxy.test.ts --run
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  13 passed (13)
    Start at  21:28:11
    Duration  2.55s
  ```
  - 12 pre-existing tests pass unchanged (existing `vi.stubGlobal("fetch")` mocks still hit because `fetchWithSsrFGuard` falls back to `globalThis.fetch` when no `fetchImpl` is supplied, and the mock has the `.mock` shape the guard detects for hermetic test mode).
  - 1 new test (`routes the request through the SSRF guard with the operator-allowed proxy host`) drives `streamProxy` against a real `http.createServer` on `127.0.0.1:<port>` and asserts:
    - exactly one POST reached `/api/stream`,
    - `Authorization: Bearer token-abc` was forwarded,
    - the JSON body's `model.id` and `model.provider` match the input,
    - `options.headers` was scrubbed (the existing `sanitizeProxyModel` + `buildProxyRequestOptions` contract is preserved).
- **Observed result after fix**: Real loopback request flows end-to-end through the guard's pinned-dispatcher branch (no `vi.stubGlobal`), and the response is fully consumed before `releaseGuarded()` returns. Reverting either the `fetchWithSsrFGuard` wrap or the `policy.allowedHostnames` line makes the inline test fail (the guard would reject the loopback hostname as a private IP, or `sanitizeProxyModel` would leak `headers`).
- **What was not tested**: Live POST against a real proxy deployment; the proof is unit-level via the production constructor + loopback, the same shape approved for prior fetch-guard wiring PRs.

## Out of scope (separate follow-ups)

- `src/agents/provider-local-service.ts:232` (`probeHealth`) — sibling surface with the same pattern, submitted as a separate PR to keep each change XS.
- `src/agents/minimax-vlm.ts` and `src/infra/push-apns.relay.ts` — additional unguarded outgoing fetch sites identified during exploration; tracked as future SSRF-wiring PRs.

## Risk

- **Scope**: 1 prod file + 1 test file; +19 source LoC (net) + 53 test LoC.
- **Behavior**: Same outgoing request shape as before, plus 1 new `fetchWithSsrFGuard` option-object pass. `streamProxy`'s public signature, return shape, and event stream are unchanged.
- **No API/signature changes**: The change is entirely internal to `streamProxy`'s request path; downstream consumers (e.g. `buildGuardedModelFetch`) are untouched.
- **Compatibility**: All 12 pre-existing tests in `proxy.test.ts` still pass because `fetchWithSsrFGuard` falls back to `globalThis.fetch` when no `fetchImpl` is supplied, and the existing `vi.stubGlobal("fetch", vi.fn(...))` mocks keep working (the guard detects them as mocked fetch and skips real DNS pinning).
- **Type check**: `pnpm tsgo` clean on the touched branch.
- **Sibling coordination**: Distinct file from `provider-local-service.ts`; submitted as a separate PR.

target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip plugin bootstrap and bundled fallback during delivery target resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a heartbeat wake-loop latency regression where delivery-target resolution blocks for ~60s per tick when the configured channel plugin is not already in the active runtime registry.

### Background

Commit [`6470bb7625`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6470bb7625) introduced `allowBootstrap: true` in heartbeat delivery-target resolution so plugin channel targets could be loaded on demand. However, `resolveRuntimePluginRegistry()` scans **all** installed plugins — not just the target channel.

### Root cause

`bootstrapAttempts` guard in `channel-bootstrap.runtime.ts`:
- **Success**: key cached → subsequent ticks skip
- **Failure** (plugin not installed / config issue): key deleted → every tick re-scans

## Changes

1. **Hot path**: heartbeat call sites pass `allowBootstrap: false, allowBundledFallback: false`
2. **Startup pre-activation**: `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins()` loads external plugins once before heartbeat loop
3. **Per-agent coverage**: iterates `agents.list[].heartbeat` entries (matching `resolveHeartbeatConfig` merge semantics)
4. **Session-derived `target:last`**: keeps guarded bootstrap (not pre-activatable from config)
5. **Hot reload & override preactivation**: `updateConfig` and `requestHeartbeat` (cron/manual wakes) call preactivation so externally-configured targets introduced after startup are covered
6. **Doctor caller compatibility**: `allowBootstrap` parameter threaded through `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget` so doctor (which runs outside the wake loop) can resolve external plugin targets without preactivation
7. **Test coverage**: mock-backed assertions in `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts` verifying external-target resolution, standard-channel skip, dedup, and distinct-target branches

## Evidence

### Test proof

```
pnpm test src/infra/outbound/heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts src/infra/outbound/targets.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts
```
131/131 tests pass across 3 test files (19 + 87 + 25).

### Real gateway proof

Production config (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`), heartbeat `every=30s target=qqbot`, no `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS` — real gateway process with qqbot/feishu channels connected.

Gateway startup:
```
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [gateway] http server listening (12 plugins…)
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [gateway] ready
2026-07-06T11:46:xx [heartbeat] started
```

Proof event timeline (appendFileSync probes, reverted from source before commit):
```
[gateway]  pre-activate: target=qqbot isExternal=false  → standard channel no-op 1ms
[heartbeat] main-plugin resolve: channel=qqbot→qqbot in 0ms (no bootstrap)
[heartbeat] session-route resolve: channel=qqbot→qqbot in 0ms (no bootstrap)
[heartbeat] TICK COMPLETE: agent=test_agent channel=qqbot to=proof-test-target totalMs=3
```

## Revision (2026-07-06)

Addressed ClawSweeper review findings:

- **P1 — reload gap**: `updateConfig()` in heartbeat runner now calls `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` before rebuilding the agent schedule
- **P1 — override gap**: `requestHeartbeat()` wake handler pre-activates requested-heartbeat override targets before the no-bootstrap resolver runs
- **P1 — doctor regression**: `resolveHeartbeatDeliveryTarget` accepts `allowBootstrap?: boolean` so the doctor path (which runs outside the wake loop without preactivation) can still resolve external plugin targets
- **Test assertions**: `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts` now uses mocked `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin` with real assertions (call count, `allowBootstrap: true`, standard-channel skip, dedup)
- Kept existing `target:last` guarded bootstrap unchanged

## Revision (2026-07-07) #1

Removed duplicate heartbeat plugin preactivation path identified by ClawSweeper review:

- **P2 — duplicate startup preactivation**: Removed `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` from `activateGatewayScheduledServices`. The `startHeartbeatRunner` constructor already calls `updateConfig(state.cfg)` which handles the initial preactivation plus all hot-reload/config-update paths. Removing the gateway-side call eliminates a repeated registry scan when an external target fails to load.
- Updated comment in `heartbeat-runner.ts` `updateConfig` to reflect it is now the single preactivation path.
- 147 related tests pass (`server-runtime-services.test.ts`, `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts`, `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, `targets.test.ts`).

## Revision (2026-07-07) #2 (a0ba292)

Addressed ClawSweeper [P2] finding — gating preactivation to enabled, deliverable heartbeat configs:

**Problem**: `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins` was called from `updateConfig` before the interval filter (`resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs`). A disabled heartbeat config (`every: "0m"`) with an external target still triggered `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` during startup/reload, scanning all installed plugins unnecessarily. External targets without a recipient (`to`) were also preactivated even though the runner can never deliver to them.

**Fix in `heartbeat-pre-activate.ts`**:
- Config-scan path (startup/reload): each target is only preactivated when the heartbeat is enabled (`resolveHeartbeatIntervalMs` returns non-null) AND has a deliverable recipient (`to` is set). This mirrors the `updateConfig` scheduling loop which skips agents with `intervalMs === 0`.
- Direct heartbeat override path (cron/manual wakes via `requestHeartbeat`): still preactivates without an interval check because the caller already validated the wake is active. Only skips targets without a recipient.

**New regression tests** (+7 in `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`):
- ✅ Disabled default (`every: "0m"`) → no preactivation
- ✅ Disabled per-agent (`every: "0m"`) → no preactivation
- ✅ Missing `to` on default target → no preactivation
- ✅ Missing `to` on per-agent target → no preactivation
- ✅ Missing `to` on heartbeat override → no preactivation
- ✅ Per-agent with its own `every: "15m"` overrides disabled default → preactivated

**Test results**: 19/19 `heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts`, 87/87 `targets.test.ts`, 25/25 `heartbeat-runner.scheduler.test.ts` — all pass.

target.title: [AI] fix(embedding): retry without dimensions and degrade non-local providers on persistent failure
target.body:
## Summary

Self-hosted OpenAI-compatible embedding servers (llama.cpp, Ollama, vLLM, TGI, Alibaba) that reject the OpenAI `dimensions` parameter caused memory indexing to hang indefinitely in an infinite retry loop. Non-local embedding providers also lacked a degradation path, preventing FTS-only fallback.

- Problem: `postEmbeddingRequest` always sends `dimensions` when configured → self-hosted servers reject/reset → infinite retry loop (3 retries × batch splitting) with no graceful exit. `markLocalEmbeddingProviderDegraded` only handles `provider.id === "local"`, so non-local providers never enter FTS fallback.
- Solution: (1) Retry without `dimensions` after HTTP 4xx rejection or connection reset, with per-client circuit breaker to skip dimensions on subsequent requests. (2) Extend provider degradation to non-local providers in optional mode, allowing FTS-only fallback while preserving fail-closed for explicitly required providers.
- What changed: `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.ts` (+86/-34 — dimensions retry + circuit breaker), `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.ts` (+40/-8 — non-local provider degradation), `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts` (+57/-0 — dimensions retry test)
- What did NOT change: Local provider degradation path, retry parameters, timeout durations, cache identity computation, required-mode provider fail-closed contract, batch logging (already in main via #94732)

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #93312
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When `memorySearch.provider` is set to `openai-compatible` with `outputDimensionality` pointing at a self-hosted embedding server (llama.cpp, Ollama, vLLM, TGI, Alibaba DashScope, etc.), the server typically rejects the OpenAI-specific `dimensions` parameter with HTTP 400 or resets the connection. Since `postEmbeddingRequest` always includes `dimensions`, every retry fails identically. The outer `runMemoryEmbeddingBatchRetryWithSplit` retries 3 times with exponential backoff, then recursively halves and retries — all with the same failing payload. The process loops until killed by SIGKILL.

Even after retries are exhausted, `markLocalEmbeddingProviderDegraded` gates on `provider.id === "local"` and returns immediately for non-local providers. The sync error handler's graceful FTS-only path requires `!this.provider`, which never becomes true, so the error is re-thrown and the retry cycle continues.

This fix addresses both issues: the root cause (dimensions rejection) and the safety net (non-local degradation).

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

**Behavior addressed**: openai-compatible memory embedding against self-hosted servers that reject the OpenAI `dimensions` parameter. Batch embedding sends dimensions first, gets HTTP 400, retries without dimensions, and succeeds. Circuit breaker then prevents subsequent requests from wasting an attempt on the same client. Non-local optional providers degrade after persistent failures instead of looping.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8 x86_64, Node v24.13.1, OpenClaw main branch at f3106057e6, branch fix/embedding-dimensions-degrade-93312.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```
node --import tsx /tmp/proof-93312-dimensions-retry.mjs
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts --run
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-timeout.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-policy.test.ts --run
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-93312-dimensions-retry.mjs
============================================================
  Real behavior proof: openai-compatible dimensions retry
  Simulated self-hosted llama.cpp / Ollama server
============================================================
Date:       2026-07-07T02:08:31.437Z
Runtime:    Node.js v24.13.1
Server:     http://127.0.0.1:45595/v1
Config:     provider=openai-compatible model=bge-m3.gguf outputDimensionality=1024
Server:     HTTP 400 on 'dimensions', 200 without

Provider:   id=openai-compatible model=bge-m3.gguf dims=1024
Cache key:  dimensions in identity = true

--- Batch embedding (3 documents) ---
Vectors:    3 (dim 3)
[25, 27, 13]

--- Query embedding ---
Vector:     [21, 22, 23]

--- Server request log ---
  #1: batch hasDims=true n=3 → 400→retry (rejected: dims unsupported)
  #2: batch hasDims=false n=3 → 200✓ (retry without dims)
  #3: query hasDims=false n=1 → 200✓ (circuit breaker)

--- Verification ---
  [PASS] Batch sends dimensions first
  [PASS] Batch retries without dimensions (400→200)
  [PASS] Circuit breaker: query skips dimensions
  [PASS] Circuit breaker: query returns 3-dim vector
  [PASS] Batch returns 3 vectors
  [PASS] Cache includes dimensions regardless of wire
  [PASS] Exactly 3 requests total (batch 400+200, query 200)
  [PASS] All responses successful (no errors)

ALL 8 CHECKS PASSED
============================================================
```

Dimensions retry behavior matrix:

```
Request sequence                    => Result
Batch request with dimensions       => HTTP 400 → retry without dimensions → HTTP 200
Query request (after circuit breaker) => skips dimensions → HTTP 200 (1 request, not 2)
Cache identity                      => includes dimensions regardless of wire behavior
```

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  27 passed (27)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-timeout.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-embedding-policy.test.ts --run
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  37 passed (37)
```

**Observed result after fix**:
1. Production `postEmbeddingRequest` sends `dimensions` on first attempt (compatible endpoints unchanged)
2. On HTTP 400 with "Unrecognized request parameter: dimensions", retries without dimensions and succeeds
3. Circuit breaker (WeakSet) prevents subsequent requests from sending dimensions to the same client
4. Provider identity (`dimensions` in `cacheKeyData`) preserved regardless of wire retry
5. Non-local optional providers (auto, local transport) degrade after persistent failures, enabling FTS-only fallback
6. Required providers (explicitly configured non-local) preserve fail-closed semantics
7. 64 tests pass (27 + 37), 8/8 proof checks pass

**What was not tested**: Live llama.cpp GPU server with BGE-M3 model (requires Intel Arc A770 not available in this environment). Alibaba Cloud text-embedding-v3 end-to-end (requires cloud credentials). Full multi-file memory index of 665 workspace files (requires full OpenClaw workspace + GPU server). The unit tests cover the exact code paths from the bug report; the proof script validates the retry + circuit breaker behavior with a real HTTP server on the production provider-adapter code path.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

**Cause 1 — dimensions always sent**: `postEmbeddingRequest` (openai-compatible-embedding-provider.ts:356) unconditionally includes `dimensions` when configured, with no retry-without path. Introduced by PR #85269 (dutifulbob) which added the OpenAI-compatible embedding provider. Made visible by user reports with self-hosted llama.cpp/Ollama endpoints that reject unknown parameters.

**Cause 2 — non-local degradation missing**: `markLocalEmbeddingProviderDegraded` (manager.ts:516) gates on `this.provider?.id !== "local"` and returns early for all non-local providers. The sync error handler (manager-sync-ops.ts:2582) requires `!this.provider` for graceful FTS-only exit, which never becomes true for non-local providers.

**Confidence**: clear — both causes are confirmed by source inspection of current main (f3106057e6).

## Regression Test Plan

- Target: `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts` (27 tests), `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/embeddings.test.ts`, `manager-embedding-timeout.test.ts`, `manager-embedding-policy.test.ts` (37 tests)
- New test "retries without dimensions when the server rejects the parameter" validates: dimensions sent first → 400 → retry without dimensions → success; circuit breaker on subsequent requests; provider identity preserved
- Existing local-provider degradation tests unchanged
- 64 total tests pass, 0 regressions

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None by default. Self-hosted embedding endpoints that previously hung will now complete successfully. The dimensions retry is transparent — compatible endpoints still receive dimensions on the first request. The only observable change is that previously-hanging memory indexes now complete.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No (same endpoint, retry without one JSON field)
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Real HTTP server simulating llama.cpp dimensions rejection → retry → success; circuit breaker prevents second dimensions attempt; cache identity preserved; existing local provider degradation unchanged
- Edge cases checked: Dimensions configured but not in circuit breaker → sent first; already in circuit breaker → skipped; no dimensions configured → no retry needed; signal aborted → no retry; required-mode provider → no degradation
- What you did NOT verify: Live GPU-powered llama.cpp with BGE-M3; full workspace memory index of 665 files end-to-end; provider close() side effects after non-local degradation

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes (compatible endpoints still receive dimensions; incompatible endpoints now succeed instead of hanging)
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — The dimensions retry is at the right boundary (provider adapter handles endpoint compatibility). The degradation extension is at the right boundary (memory manager owns provider lifecycle). Both follow existing patterns: the retry is modeled on the outer `runMemoryEmbeddingBatchRetryWithSplit`; the degradation reuses the existing `createDegradedMemoryProviderLifecycle` infrastructure.
- **Refactor needed**: No — The embedding provider architecture already has the degraded/lifecycle infrastructure; we simply close two gaps (no dimensions retry, no non-local degradation).
- **Alternative considered**: (1) Remove dimensions entirely — would break compatible endpoints that produce the correct output dimensionality. (2) Add a config flag per provider — unnecessary complexity; circuit breaker handles this transparently. (3) Broader approach with committed proof script — the proof script in repository adds unnecessary surface; we keep proof external.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: deepseek-v4-pro
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest-risk area**: The dimensions retry could mask genuinely misconfigured endpoints — if a server rejects dimensions for a reason other than parameter incompatibility, the retry might succeed silently with wrong-dimensionality vectors.

**Mitigations**:
- Retry is capped at 1 per request (the outer memory embedding retry loop provides independent exponential backoff with `maxAttempts=3`)
- Circuit breaker is per-client, per-process (WeakSet) — no persistent state, resets on restart
- Error detection regex covers 6+ provider families with conservative matching
- AbortSignal propagation ensures caller cancellation wins
- Required-mode providers still fail-closed (no silent degradation)

**Compatibility impact**: No breaking changes. Compatible endpoints receive dimensions as before. Incompatible endpoints now succeed instead of hanging. Existing configurations work without modification.

---

Related to #93312

target.title: feat(line): per-user in-flight guard for concurrent message errors
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves When LINE users send rapid consecutive messages, the second message hits session lock timeouts or command queue contention, resulting in a generic "⚠️ Something went wrong" error after a long wait. The user gets no feedback for minutes, then sees an unhelpful error. ## Why This Change Was Made Instead of letting concurrent messages fail after a timeout, this adds a lightweight per-user in-flight guard at the LINE webhook handler level. When the same user's previous message is still being processed, the guard immediately sends a "⏳ still processing" reply and skips the duplicate, preventing the downstream concurrency conflict entirely. ## User Impact **This changes default LINE delivery semantics**: rapid follow-up events from the *same user* now get an immediate busy reply and are skipped, instead of dispatching concurrently and failing with a late timeout error. The guard is wired by default in `createLineBot`. - Users sending rapid messages get immediate "⏳ Your previous message is still being processed…" feedback instead of a timeout error - The guard only applies to events with a stable sender identity. `@line/bot-sdk` marks source `userId` optional (group/room postbacks and non-mobile group senders arrive without it), so senderless events bypass the guard and keep today's concurrent dispatch — one user's in-flight message can never block another user's button tap or message - Different users in the same group are isolated (guard key = account | conversation | user) - Guard releases on both success and error (try/finally), so a failed message never permanently blocks the user ## Evidence **Unit tests** — 35/35 pass (`pnpm test extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.test.ts`), covering: busy reply delivery, guard release after success/error, per-user isolation in groups, and regressions for senderless group postbacks/messages bypassing the guard. **Review findings addressed** (from the earlier Codex review): - Senderless postback cross-blocking: `buildLineInFlightKey` now returns `null` when `source.userId` is absent and the guard is skipped, so senderless group/room postbacks keep main's concurrent dispatch instead of collapsing onto one `unknown` key - The previous PR body incorrectly described the guard as opt-in; it is wired by default in `createLineBot` and the User Impact section above now states the delivery-semantics change explicitly - Rebased onto current `main`; conflicts resolved **Real LINE behavior proof** — captured on a live LINE Messaging API bot running this branch (commit `a3af9cd299`, since rebased to `5a59a2cbd6` with no code changes; gateway run from source, webhook via public tunnel). ## 1. Busy reply on rapid same-user messages (1:1 chat) Two messages sent back-to-back; the second immediately received the busy reply, then the first message's real answer arrived: ## 2. Same-group isolation + guard release (group chat) One group, two human users (green bubbles = user A, bee avatar = user B, penguin avatar = the bot): - 12:40 user A mentions the bot with a first message (processing takes ~10s) - 12:41 user A sends a rapid follow-up → gets the ⏳ busy reply (same-user guard) - user B's message sent during user A's processing is **not** blocked — no busy reply, normal answer (per-user isolation) - user A's later message is answered normally (guard released after completion) ## 3. Redacted gateway log timeline Guard-skipped messages never reach dispatch, so the second rapid message from the same user has no `message received` entry, while both distinct-user group messages do: ```text # 1:1 — first message dispatched and processed; the rapid second message was # guard-skipped before dispatch (no "message received" entry; busy reply in screenshot 1) 2026-07-06T12:35:47.495+08:00 [diagnostic] message received: channel=line chatId=line:U[redacted-user-A] messageId=621564378994966788 ... 2026-07-06T12:35:56.033+08:00 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=line chatId=line:U[redacted-user-A] messageId=621564378994966788 outcome=completed duration=8537ms # group — two messages from two different users overlap; BOTH are dispatched # (different guard keys), the second queues and completes; no cross-user busy reply 2026-07-06T12:40:59.427+08:00 [diagnostic] message received: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564906756113015 ... 2026-07-06T12:41:00.868+08:00 [diagnostic] message received: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564907796299863 ... 2026-07-06T12:41:09.310+08:00 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564906756113015 outcome=completed duration=9881ms 2026-07-06T12:41:14.974+08:00 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564907796299863 outcome=completed duration=14099ms # group — user A's later message after guard release, answered normally 2026-07-06T12:41:16.583+08:00 [diagnostic] message received: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564936065122495 ... 2026-07-06T12:41:21.625+08:00 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=line chatId=line:group:C[redacted-group] messageId=621564936065122495 outcome=completed duration=5042ms ``` User IDs, group ID, and session IDs are redacted. This PR supersedes openclaw/openclaw#96379 (same commits, resubmitted from this account); full review history and the original evidence comment are there.

target.title: fix(msteams): add graphMediaFallback so group-chat file attachments reach the agent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Files attached to Microsoft Teams **group chat** messages never reach the agent, even with all recommended Graph Application permissions granted (#89594). Teams strips the `<attachment id="…">` tags from the message HTML it delivers to bots in group chats, so `extractMSTeamsHtmlAttachmentIds` returns an empty list and the existing Graph media fallback in `resolveMSTeamsInboundMedia` never fires. The Graph copy of the same message retains both the tag and the full `reference` attachment (SharePoint `contentUrl` + name), so the already-implemented `downloadMSTeamsGraphMedia` path works fine once it is allowed to run — the gate is the only blocker.

Verified discrepancy on a live tenant (same message, `19:…@thread.v2` group chat, plugin 2026.6.11):

- Bot Framework activity: one `text/html` attachment, plugin diagnostics `{'htmlAttachments': 1, 'attachmentTags': 0, 'attachmentIds': []}`
- Graph `GET /chats/{chatId}/messages/{messageId}`: body HTML contains `<attachment id="…"></attachment>` and `attachments: [{ contentType: "reference", contentUrl: "https://…sharepoint.com/…/file.pdf", name: "file.pdf" }]`

## Why This Change Was Made

The gate exists for a good reason — mention-only group messages also arrive as `text/html` attachments, and keying on contentType alone caused spurious Graph lookups and 404 diagnostics (#58617). So instead of relaxing the gate unconditionally, this adds an explicit opt-in:

`channels.msteams.graphMediaFallback` (default: `false`) — for **group-chat** conversations that carried a `text/html` attachment and yielded no media, attempt the Graph message fetch even when no `<attachment id>` tags were extracted. **Channel (team-scope) conversations are excluded** and keep the tag-gated behavior: the channel Graph URL builder has separate known team-GUID and reply-URL defects (per ClawSweeper review, tracked with the broader channel repair in #90738), so this flag must not route channel traffic into that path.

- Default `false`: behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged, including the #58617 protection (covered by existing tests, which still pass unmodified).
- Enabled: costs one Graph message lookup per group-chat message that yields no downloadable media (including mention-only messages) — the trade-off is documented in `docs/channels/msteams.md`. Requires `Chat.Read.All` and `Files.Read.All` Application permissions with admin consent.
- Personal (Bot Framework `a:`/`8:orgid:`) chats are unaffected — they keep the Bot Framework v3 attachments path.

## User Impact

Operators whose agents live in Teams group chats can enable one config flag and file attachments (PDFs, docs, images uploaded as files) become readable by the agent. Channel (team-scope) attachment behavior is intentionally unchanged — that repair lands separately (#90738). Everyone else sees no change.

## Evidence

- Live validation: an equivalent gate relaxation applied to a production 2026.6.11 install (macOS, single-tenant bot) — a PDF attached to a group-chat message was fetched via the Graph reference path (`downloaded attachments {'count': 1}`) and the agent answered questions about its content. Before the change, the same message produced `graph fallback never attempted` (extraction all-zero) and the agent saw no file.
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/inbound-media.test.ts` — 16 passed (12 existing unmodified + 4 new: enabled-flag group fetch, default-off unchanged, personal-chat exclusion, channel-conversation exclusion)
- `pnpm test:extension msteams` — 70 files, 999 tests passed
- `pnpm check` — clean
- `pnpm test:contracts:channels` — 34 passed

Relates to #89594 — fixes the **group-chat** variant with live proof. Channel-specific root causes (team GUID, reply-URL shape; #90733 analysis) are intentionally left to the broader channel repair (#90738), so this PR does not close the canonical issue.

target.title: fix(proxy-capture): guard body-less arrayBuffer reads against oversized responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `readCapturedResponseBodyBounded` in the proxy capture runtime would buffer the full response body through `arrayBuffer()` before checking the byte cap when the cloned response lacks a streaming body. A response with an oversized declared `content-length` would still be fully allocated in memory before the post-read check discarded it, violating the function's bounded-read contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

The body-less fallback path (reachable with non-standard Response clones) now checks the `content-length` header before calling `arrayBuffer()`. When the declared length exceeds `maxBytes`, the function returns `{ truncated: true }` immediately without materializing the body. The stream path (normal ReadableStream clones) already enforced the cap correctly via chunked reading with `reader.cancel()`.

## User Impact

Operators running the debug proxy capture with large or hostile provider responses get the same OOM guard in the body-less path that already exists in the stream path. No config or API surface changes.

## Evidence

**Environment:** Node.js v24, real `readCapturedResponseBodyBounded` exported function. Body-less fallback tests use mock clones (`body: null`) to force the `!body` branch; stream-path tests use real `Response` objects.

**After fix — body-less fallback tests (mock clone, 3 cases):**

```
[case 1] content-length exceeds cap: returns truncated, arrayBuffer() NOT called
  ok: truncated
  ok: buffer empty
  ok: arrayBuffer spy not called
[case 2] content-length within cap: falls through to arrayBuffer(), returns body
  ok: not truncated
  ok: body matches
  ok: arrayBuffer called once
[case 3] missing content-length, within cap: falls through to arrayBuffer()
  ok: not truncated
  ok: body matches
  ok: arrayBuffer called once
```

**After fix — stream path tests (real Response, 3 cases):**

```
[case 4] content-length within cap: returns body
  ok: not truncated | ok: body matches
[case 5] missing content-length, within cap: returns body
  ok: not truncated | ok: body matches
[case 6] stream body within cap: returns body (regression guard)
  ok: not truncated | ok: correct size
```

**Negative control (content-length precheck removed, same tests, same environment):**

```
FAIL: skips body read when content-length exceeds cap (body-less fallback)
TypeError: The first argument must be of type string or an instance of Buffer...
  → arrayBuffer() was called (returned undefined), guard is proven load-bearing
```

**Focused tests:**

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/runtime.test.ts
Tests  14 passed (14)  (8 existing + 6 new)
```

**Lint/format:** `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on changed files.

target.title: feat(gateway): add global auth rate limit mode for IP-agnostic brute-force protection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw is deployed with `gateway.bind: "lan"` (or behind a reverse proxy exposing it to the public internet) and uses `gateway.auth.mode: "password"`, the current auth rate limiter only tracks failures per `{scope, clientIp}`. An attacker who can rotate IPs (proxy pools, botnets, cloud instances) gets a fresh counter for each IP, effectively bypassing the rate limit entirely.

This PR adds an optional `gateway.auth.rateLimit.global` flag that, when enabled, counts failed attempts across all client IPs in one shared counter per auth scope, so rotating-IP brute-force attacks cannot bypass the limiter.

Fixes #101255

## Why This Change Was Made

The implementation is minimal and opt-in:

- `RateLimitConfig` interface and `GatewayAuthRateLimitConfig` type: add `global?: boolean` (default `false`)
- `createAuthRateLimiter`: `resolveKey` drops the IP component when global mode is enabled, so all IPs share the same `${scope}` counter
- Zod schema: accept `global` in the strict rateLimit config object
- `exemptLoopback` still applies independently in global mode, so local CLI access is not affected by a remote attack triggering a global lockout

## User Impact

- **No existing behavior changes**: default remains `false` (per-IP tracking) for full backward compatibility
- Operators who set `global: true` get IP-agnostic brute-force protection for public-exposed deployments
- Tradeoff documented: a global bucket means a flood from any IP can lock out all clients for that auth scope

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/auth-rate-limit.test.ts`: **172 passed** (existing 43×4 suites + 9 new global-mode test cases)
- New tests cover: shared counter across IPs, lockout propagation, scope isolation, loopback exemption, reset, maxEntries interaction, backward-compat default, and retryAfterMs for arbitrary IPs
- All 4 gateway test suites pass: `|gateway-core|`, `|gateway-server|`, `|gateway-client|`, `|gateway-methods|`

target.title: fix(telegram): add UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT to PRE_CONNECT_ERROR_CODES
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`isSafeToRetrySendError` guards non-idempotent `sendMessage` retries by checking only `PRE_CONNECT_ERROR_CODES` — errors that are guaranteed to have occurred *before* the request reached Telegram's servers. `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` (undici's TCP/TLS connect timeout) was not in this set, so `sendMessage` would not retry when the connection timed out during the handshake.

This is inconsistent: `ECONNREFUSED`, `ENOTFOUND`, `ENETUNREACH`, and `EHOSTUNREACH` are all in `PRE_CONNECT_ERROR_CODES` because they fire before the connection is established. `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` has the same property — it fires during TCP/TLS connect, before any HTTP request bytes are written to the socket — yet it was only in `RECOVERABLE_ERROR_CODES` (permissive, for idempotent operations).

## Why This Change Was Made

undici's connect timeout covers the TCP three-way handshake and TLS negotiation phases. The HTTP request data is only written after the connection is established. If the connect timer fires, no bytes were sent — meaning Telegram never received the message, and retrying is safe.

Adding `"UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT"` to `PRE_CONNECT_ERROR_CODES` makes `isSafeToRetrySendError` consistent with its contract: retry only when the message was definitely not delivered.

| undici error code | Phase | Request sent? | Safe to retry sendMessage? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` | TCP/TLS connect | ❌ | **Yes (FIX)** |
| `UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT` | Response headers | ✅ | ❌ |
| `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT` | Response body | ✅ | ❌ |

## User Impact

`sendMessage` becomes more resilient on flaky networks — connection timeouts during the TCP/TLS handshake will be retried instead of failing the send. No risk of duplicate messages because the connect timeout guarantees no request data was transmitted.

## Evidence

Verified against commit `02892535` on branch `fix/telegram-pre-connect-undici-timeout`.

### Before (broken)

```
err=UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT (never sent — should retry)
    isSafeToRetrySendError  => false FAIL
```

### After (fixed)

```
err=UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT (never sent — should retry)
    isSafeToRetrySendError  => true  PASS
```

### Regression guard

```
err=UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT (response headers — request already sent)
    isSafeToRetrySendError  => false PASS (unchanged)

err=UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT (response body — request already sent)
    isSafeToRetrySendError  => false PASS (unchanged)

err=ECONNRESET (connection reset — ambiguous)
    isSafeToRetrySendError  => false PASS (unchanged)

err=ETIMEDOUT (ambiguous)
    isSafeToRetrySendError  => false PASS (unchanged)
```

## Tests and Validation

```
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/network-errors.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       58 passed (58)
```

One assertion updated: `UND_ERR_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` now expects `true` for `isSafeToRetrySendError`, matching all other pre-connect error codes.

## Risk Checklist

- **User-visible behavior:** No — `sendMessage` retries on one additional error code that is guaranteed to fire before any data reaches Telegram.
- **Config/env/migration behavior:** No.
- **Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution:** No.
- **Plugins/providers/channels/SDK:** No — internal to Telegram plugin.
- **Highest-risk area:** None. Adding a pre-connect error code to the pre-connect set is mechanically consistent. The undici error code is well-defined in Node.js internals.
- **Mitigation:** Existing tests (58) + updated regression assertion; all other undici error codes remain excluded from the pre-connect set.

Closes: N/A

target.title: fix: block WhatsApp direct sends during reachout timelock
target.body:
Related: #100971

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp direct-message sends could be handed to Baileys and reported as locally accepted even when the account was under a WhatsApp reachout timelock that blocks outgoing direct chats.

That made the failure show up late and indirectly through Baileys/WhatsApp delivery errors instead of failing before OpenClaw attempted the send.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix keeps the behavior owned by the WhatsApp plugin and uses Baileys' public reachout-timelock surface instead of importing private token helpers or adding core/provider policy. Before direct 1:1 sends, the active listener checks `connection.update.reachoutTimeLock` or refreshes `fetchAccountReachoutTimelock()` and blocks the send before `sock.sendMessage` when the timelock is active.

Group and newsletter sends are not broadened into this account-level direct-message guard. The outbound API also runs the readiness check before sending composing presence, so known-blocked direct sends fail without showing typing first.

## User Impact

WhatsApp users now get an immediate, explicit failure when their account is temporarily blocked from starting direct chats, instead of seeing a send appear accepted and then fail later through lower-level transport diagnostics.

This does not change core provider acceptance semantics, does not add config, and does not write or duplicate WhatsApp trusted-contact token state.

target.title: fix(codex-supervisor): suppress unhandled stdout/stderr stream errors in JsonRpcClient
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`JsonRpcClient.start()` attaches `data` listeners to `this.proc.stdout` and `this.proc.stderr`, but does not attach `error` listeners. If either stream emits an `error` event, the unhandled error can crash the OpenClaw process.

## Why This Change Was Made

target.title: feat(subagents): native announceTarget for subagent completion routing (#27445)
target.body:
Fixes #27445

## What Problem This Solves

Native `sessions_spawn` subagent completions always announce to the channel via delivery-mirror. Orchestrator patterns need the completion to come back to the **parent session** as a normal trigger message instead — without any direct channel announce — so the parent can integrate results and decide what (if anything) the user sees. Current parent handoff behavior exists but is hard-coded by activity/thread state, not caller-selectable, and thread-bound `mode:"session"` spawns can register no completion announce at all.

## Fix

Adds native `announceTarget: "channel" | "parent"` to `sessions_spawn` (default `"channel"`, current behavior unchanged):

- `"parent"` wakes the requester session once with `deliver:false` through the existing `subagent_announce` internal-event path — no direct channel announce, no fallback to channel on parent failure
- Thread-bound `thread:true, mode:"session"` spawns with `announceTarget:"parent"` keep direct child-thread delivery for the active run but now register completion (addresses the edge raised in the issue comments)
- Config precedence: per-spawn arg > `agents.list[].subagents.announceTarget` > `agents.defaults.subagents.announceTarget` > `"channel"`
- `announceTarget` persists in the subagent registry (JSON + SQLite) so pending completions after restart follow the original routing
- ACP `streamTo` stays separate; `announceTarget` is native-only and never maps to ACP streaming

## Evidence

- New/updated tests: spawn tool schema, spawn registration (incl. thread-bound cases), announce delivery routing (parent `deliver:false`, no channel fallback, idempotent retries), config schema precedence — all pass
- Full local `check:changed` (CI lane, `CI=1`) passes at branch head: lint, prod/test types, boundary guards, import cycles
- `config:docs:gen`/`check` clean; generated config reference updated

target.title: fix(ports): ignore malformed lsof listener pids
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a listener-diagnostics bug where malformed `lsof -F` `p` records could still attach subsequent `n` address lines to a listener entry with no valid PID. That could surface bogus busy-port diagnostics from corrupted or partial `lsof` output instead of reporting only real listening processes.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/infra/ports-inspect.ts` now accepts only positive parsed PIDs from `lsof` process records and skips listener address rows that are not attached to a valid process. This keeps the diagnostics path aligned with the stricter PID validation already used in nearby port-inspection code.

## User Impact

Gateway port diagnostics now ignore malformed `lsof` process rows instead of showing phantom listeners with missing or invalid process identity. Valid listener output is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Unit Tests
Fresh focused test runs on commit 16369d50 (after the latest manual `main` merge into this branch):

```bash
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/ports.test.ts src/cli/program.force.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8 /home/0668000995/10288592/git-hub/test/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
   Start at  09:35:28
   Duration  1.17s (transform 700ms, setup 604ms, import 29ms, tests 301ms, environment 0ms)

[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8 /home/0668000995/10288592/git-hub/test/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  22 passed (22)
   Start at  09:35:35
   Duration  1.17s (transform 678ms, setup 491ms, import 192ms, tests 161ms, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 19.99s
```

Coverage called out by Codex is present on the current branch head:
- `src/infra/ports.test.ts` keeps the repeated-listener dedupe test
- `src/infra/ports.test.ts` rejects malformed diagnostics tokens like `p111abc`
- `src/cli/program.force.test.ts` rejects malformed force-free tokens like `p111abc`

### Real Behavior Proof (for ClawSweeper/Codex)

The earlier review correctly flagged that mocked Vitest output alone was not enough. Below is a fresh real run from the current branch head, executing the production parser helper directly with `tsx` and no test harness mocks.

```bash
$ node --import tsx ./tmp-pid-proof.mjs
=== Real production code execution (no mocks) ===
Legacy behavior:  Number.parseInt("111abc", 10) = 111
Fixed behavior:   parseStrictPositiveInteger("111abc") = undefined

Legacy behavior would have accepted pid 111 from a corrupted lsof "p" record.
Fixed behavior correctly returns undefined so the record is dropped.
```

The code path now used by diagnostics is `src/infra/ports-inspect.ts:53-56`:

```typescript
if (line.startsWith("p")) {
  const pid = parseStrictPositiveInteger(line.slice(1));
  processFields = pid !== undefined ? { pid } : {};
}
```

The sibling force-free parser is hardened the same way in `src/cli/ports.ts:148-153`, so both lsof `p`-field surfaces now reject digit-prefixed garbage instead of truncating it to a valid PID.

**Result:** a malformed token like `p111abc` no longer becomes pid `111` on either path. Diagnostics drop the listener record, and `gateway run --force` no longer risks signaling the wrong process because of `parseInt` truncation.

**Current coverage summary:**
- Valid PIDs (positive integers) → accepted
- Empty/missing pid record (`p`) → skipped
- Garbage token (`pabc`) → skipped
- Trailing-garbage token (`p111abc`) → skipped on both diagnostics and force-free paths
- Repeated identical listener records for one process/address → deduplicated
- Address rows without a valid PID context → ignored

target.title: fix(cron): preserve cron context in session entry for async completion wakes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99919

When a cron job uses an async media generation tool (`image_generate`, `video_generate`, `music_generate`), the cron run ends while the media task is still in progress. When the media task later completes and wakes the session, the resumed agent run **loses the original cron context**:

- `provider` / `model` — falls back to account defaults instead of the cron's configured model
- `thinkLevel` — not restored
- `bootstrapContextRunKind` — missing; the resumed agent doesn't know it is a cron run

The agent wakes up, sees only "image done" with no memory of the original multi-step task (build → commit → deploy → notify), replies once, and ends. The remaining steps silently dead-end with `NO_REPLY`.

Additionally, the in-process gateway dispatch in `runAnnounceAgentCall` was not authorized to pass model overrides on the synthetic client. Even with the correct `provider`/`model` fields in the agent params, the gateway's `server-methods/agent` handler would reject them without `allowSyntheticModelOverride`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix has three parts:

**1. Persist** — When a cron agent run completes, write `bootstrapContextRunKind` onto the `SessionEntry` in the session store (`agent-command.ts`). This makes the cron origin discoverable by any later run on the same session key.

**2. Restore** — In `sendSubagentAnnounceDirectly`, when building the `directAgentParams` for an async completion wake, read `requesterEntry.bootstrapContextRunKind` from the loaded session entry. If it equals `"cron"`, inject `provider`, `model`, `thinking`, and `bootstrapContextRunKind` into the wake params so the resumed agent continues with the same identity.

**3. Authorize** — `runAnnounceAgentCall` now passes `allowSyntheticModelOverride: true` when the agent params carry a `provider` or `model` override. This authorizes the trusted in-process gateway dispatch so the synthetic client's model override is accepted by `server-methods/agent`, preventing the wake from being rejected before the agent resumes.

**Safety**: Only cron session entries carry `bootstrapContextRunKind: "cron"`. Subagent session entries (`agent:<id>:subagent:<uuid>`) never have this field, so subagent-to-subagent completion paths are completely unaffected. Model override authorization is only enabled when the agent params actually contain provider/model overrides.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Cron jobs using async media generation silently lost context on wake. The resumed agent had the wrong model and no memory of the task, causing multi-step jobs to dead-end after the first async call. Even after restoring provider/model in the params, the gateway could reject them.
- **After**: Async completion wakes restore the cron's provider, model, thinking level, and run kind from the persisted session entry. The in-process dispatch authorizes the model override on the synthetic client. The agent continues the original task instead of falling back to account defaults.

## Evidence

### Tests

```bash
# Targeted tests (115/115 passed, +3 tests for #99919)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts
# → 115 passed (includes 3 new tests: context injection, non-cron safety, override authorization)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/
# → 1277/1277 passed (119 test files)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.async-tasks.test.ts
# → 8/8 passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagent-announce.test.ts
# → 14/14 passed
```

### Lint

```bash
node_modules/.bin/oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.json --quiet \
  src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.ts \
  src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts
# → clean (exit 0)
```

### Review

ClawSweeper review (#101078) identified that `runAnnounceAgentCall` dispatches through `dispatchGatewayMethodInProcess` without `allowSyntheticModelOverride`, causing the gateway's `server-methods/agent` to reject provider/model overrides on the synthetic client. **Fixed in 405c9c2**.

### Revision (405c9c2)

- `runAnnounceAgentCall` now passes `allowSyntheticModelOverride: true` when the agent params include `provider` or `model` overrides, authorizing the trusted in-process dispatch path.
- New regression test (`authorizes model override on in-process dispatch when cron context includes provider/model`) uses the direct `dispatchGatewayMethodInProcess` mock (not the `callGateway` adaptation) to verify `allowSyntheticModelOverride` reaches the in-process dispatch options.
- No other callers of `runAnnounceAgentCall` pass provider/model overrides, so the authorization is only active for the cron context restoration path.

### What was tested live

- All 115 subagent-announce-delivery tests pass, including 3 new tests:
  - ✅ Cron session wake injects provider, model, thinkLevel, bootstrapContextRunKind
  - ✅ Non-cron session wake does NOT inject these fields (subagent safety)
  - ✅ `allowSyntheticModelOverride: true` is passed to `dispatchGatewayMethodInProcess` when cron context includes provider/model
- All 1277 cron tests pass unchanged
- Full lint (oxlint) pass on all changed files

### What was not tested live

- A real cron + async image_generate round-trip requires a Codex app-server environment with a live provider and is deferred to Testbox/Crabbox proof. The code-level integration tests cover the exact dispatch path (session entry → `sendSubagentAnnounceDirectly` → `directAgentParams` → `runAnnounceAgentCall` → `dispatchGatewayMethodInProcess` with `allowSyntheticModelOverride`) with mocked session store and in-process gateway dispatch.

target.title: fix(markdown-core): add CJK-friendly emphasis parsing for bold/italic
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves When agent output contains `**标签：**正文` (CJK punctuation immediately inside closing `**`), Telegram renders literal `**` instead of bold. This affects all CJK users across every channel — Chinese/Japanese/Korean LLMs frequently use the `**label：**` idiom. The root cause is markdown-it v14.3.0 strict CommonMark flanking rules: a closing `**` preceded by Unicode punctuation (full-width `：`, `。`, `、`) must be followed by whitespace/punctuation to be right-flanking. CJK text has no inter-word spaces, so the common pattern `**label：**text` never qualifies. Fixes #101120. ## Root Cause / Fix **Root cause**: markdown-it's `scanDelims` classifies CJK punctuation (Unicode category P) as punctuation, setting `right_flanking=false` for `*` delimiters adjacent to them. This prevents `**` from closing when the preceding character inside the delimiter is CJK punctuation. **Fix**: Add an inline `scanDelims` override in `createMarkdownIt` that treats CJK characters (Unicode ranges for CJK ideographs, Hangul, Kana, fullwidth forms) as word characters for emphasis flanking. When either adjacent character is CJK, allow the emphasis delimiter to both open and close. No new dependency. This is a **shared/core fix** — all channels benefit because they all consume the same markdown-core IR pipeline. **Files changed**: 1 file, +47 lines (`packages/markdown-core/src/ir.ts`) ## Evidence ### Before/After ``` === BEFORE (pure markdown-it, no CJK fix) === "**标题：**正文" => **标题：**正文 "边界：**社区显示：**Fable 与 **有效**。" => 边界：**社区显示：**Fable 与 有效。 === AFTER (with inline CJK scanDelims patch) === "**标题：**正文" => 标题：正文 "边界：**社区显示：**Fable 与 **有效**。" => 边界：社区显示：Fable 与 有效。 ``` ### Regression: non-CJK bold unchanged ``` ✅ **hello** world ✅ **foo** and **bar** ✅ this is **bold** text ✅ *italic* and **bold** ``` ## Change Type / Scope / Security Impact - **Type**: fix - **Scope**: `packages/markdown-core` (shared parser, affects all channels) - **Files**: 1 file, +47 lines - **Dependency**: None added — inline Unicode range checks, no new npm packages - **Security**: No security impact — the patch only changes emphasis flanking for CJK-adjacent delimiters - **Backward compatibility**: Non-CJK emphasis behavior unchanged (4/4 regression tests pass)

target.title: fix(proxy): add error handler on upstream response stream
target.body:
Related to #82442. The CONNECT client-socket crash reported there was fixed by #82444; this PR covers the distinct HTTP upstream-response stream failure path.

## What Problem This Solves

The debug proxy consumed upstream `IncomingMessage` bodies without an `error` listener. If an origin closed the connection after sending response headers, Node emitted a response-stream error that could become unhandled and crash the proxy.

The old candidate handler also tried to end the downstream response with the upstream error text. Once a 2xx status and partial body had already been forwarded, that would make a truncated response look complete and append diagnostic text to application data.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Record upstream response-stream failures as inbound capture errors.
- Before downstream headers are committed, return a complete generic `502 Bad Gateway` response with `Connection: close`.
- After downstream headers are committed, destroy the downstream response so clients observe an incomplete response rather than a valid partial 2xx body.
- Reuse the same terminal-response helper for request-level upstream failures, without reflecting upstream error strings to clients.
- Preserve current body-preview capture behavior and current managed-proxy policy.

This follows Node's documented HTTP lifecycle: a premature upstream close after the response begins emits `aborted`/`close`/`error` on the incoming response, while destroying an outgoing response closes its socket. See the [Node HTTP documentation](https://nodejs.org/api/http.html).

## User Impact

Broken origins no longer crash the local debug proxy. Failures before headers produce a truthful 502; failures after headers terminate the partial response; the proxy remains available for subsequent requests.

## Evidence

- Exact reviewed head: `72fde9717fb6bd9e790f0ef3de77cac06c268a61`.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox run `run_246cffe1bd2b`, lease `cbx_71a6b7c8518f`, Node `v24.15.0`, public networking, no Tailscale, no instance profile.
- Command: `pnpm test src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.test.ts src/proxy-capture/proxy-server.managed-proxy.test.ts`.
- Result: 2 test files and 13 tests passed.
- Real-wire regressions prove a complete generic 502 before headers, an incomplete partial 200 after headers with no appended error text, capture-store error records for both paths, and a successful second request through the same proxy after each failure.
- Fresh pre-commit autoreview found no accepted or actionable findings.

The original contributor reproduction established the missing-listener crash surface. The maintainer rewrite keeps the contribution in this PR, preserves contributor credit, and strengthens the client-visible contract and regression proof.

target.title: fix(acp): preserve structured exec approval metadata
target.body:
## Summary

- Back ACP structured exec approval metadata with a real Gateway request contract instead of parser-only field reads.
- Allow `exec.approval.request` to carry optional `title` and `toolCallId`, store sanitized metadata on the pending approval request, and broadcast it through `exec.approval.requested`.
- Add Gateway producer and ACP translator regression coverage, including a Gateway-produced event passed into `AcpGatewayAgent.handleGatewayEvent` and resolved through the Gateway approval handler.

## What Problem This Solves

The previous patch preserved `request.title` and `request.toolCallId` in the ACP parser, but real Gateway `exec.approval.requested` events could not produce those fields because the closed Gateway request schema rejected them and the Gateway request producer did not store or broadcast them.

That made the ACP parser change a test-only contract: ACP appeared to preserve metadata that the live Gateway event path could not send.

This update makes structured `exec.approval.requested` events the source of truth for ACP permission `title` and `toolCallId` by adding the metadata at the Gateway schema, request builder, stored payload, producer, and translator test boundaries.

## User Impact

ACP clients receiving relayed Gateway exec approvals can keep the original tool-call correlation id and user-facing approval title instead of falling back to `exec:<approvalId>` and `Command approval requested` for early structured approval events.

This keeps permission prompts easier to correlate with the originating exec tool call while leaving approval decisions, allowed options, command hydration, and fallback behavior unchanged when metadata is absent.

## Origin / follow-up

- **Follows / completes:** #79337, which introduced ACP exec approval permission relay support.
- **Gap this fills:** #79337 covered the relay contract and fallback structured approval behavior; this follow-up backs structured approval metadata with the Gateway request/event source before ACP consumes it.
- **Linked issue context:** #3257 is related approval visibility/auditability context, but this PR is a narrower Gateway-to-ACP metadata contract fix and does not claim to close #3257.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- Searched open PRs for `permission-relay toolCallId title`, `exec approval metadata`, `exec.approval.requested title`, and `ACP approval metadata`; no open competing PR was found for the ACP structured exec approval metadata contract.
- #92236 is an open progress/commentary WebChat PR and does not touch ACP exec approval permission relay metadata.
- The linked issue proof prework flagged nonlocal Discord/live channel context for #3257; this PR does not claim Discord or third-party channel proof and scopes the proof to the local Gateway approval event boundary under review.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Structured Gateway exec approval events should carry and relay real `request.title` and `request.toolCallId` into ACP `session/request_permission` instead of relying on impossible parser-only fields.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw PR worktree on Linux with Node/pnpm. The proof exercises the actual Gateway `exec.approval.request` handler, `ExecApprovalManager`, Gateway broadcast payload, `AcpGatewayAgent.handleGatewayEvent`, ACP `request_permission` mapping, and Gateway `exec.approval.resolve` handler.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
env -C "/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-101037" pnpm vitest run src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests       200 passed (200)
```

The new translator regression case starts from a Gateway-produced event, not a hand-built ACP helper payload:

```text
Gateway exec.approval.request params:
  id: approval-gateway-raw
  sessionKey: agent:main:main
  title: Run echo raw
  toolCallId: tool-raw

Observed ACP permission request:
  rawInput.approvalId: approval-gateway-raw
  toolCall.toolCallId: tool-raw
  toolCall.title: Run echo raw

Observed Gateway resolution:
  exec.approval.resolve({ id: approval-gateway-raw, decision: allow-once })
```

Additional focused helper/parser regression still passes:

```text
env -C "/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-101037" pnpm vitest run src/acp/permission-relay.test.ts

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       4 passed (4)
```

Type and format gates run after the fix:

```text
env -C "/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-101037" pnpm check:test-types

pnpm tsgo:core:test and pnpm tsgo:extensions:test completed successfully.
```

```text
env -C "/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-101037" pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/exec-approvals.ts src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-request.ts src/gateway/server-methods/exec-approval.ts src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals.ts

All matched files use the correct format.
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Gateway accepts optional approval metadata, broadcasts it on the real structured `exec.approval.requested` payload, ACP uses that metadata for `request_permission`, and the selected ACP decision resolves the same Gateway approval id.
- **What was not tested:** No hosted third-party service, Discord channel, external ACP client UI, or remote CI completion is claimed here. The proof is local and targets the Gateway-to-ACP approval event boundary that the review finding identified.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause contract fix.

## Maintainer-ready details

- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the Gateway-to-ACP metadata contract under review. The patch defines optional metadata at the Gateway protocol schema, carries it through the request producer, stores it on the pending approval payload, broadcasts it in the structured approval event, and verifies ACP consumption from a Gateway-produced event.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** ACP clients can correlate the permission prompt with the original exec tool call and display the intended approval title instead of a synthetic fallback, without changing approval decisions or command execution policy.
- **Scope boundary:** This PR is limited to optional `title` and `toolCallId` metadata on Gateway exec approval requests/events and ACP permission relay consumption. It does not change channel transports, Discord proof behavior, provider execution, approval policy, or command resolution.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The source of truth is the structured `exec.approval.requested` payload produced from Gateway `record.request`. Because `buildRequestedApprovalEvent(record)` broadcasts that request unchanged, the contract belongs in `ExecApprovalRequestParamsSchema`, the host request builder, and `createExecApprovalHandlers` before ACP reads it.
- **Patch quality notes:** The diff is focused on the approval metadata contract and matching tests. The only added `.catch(reject)` is in test harness plumbing after `Promise.resolve(...)` normalizes a `void | Promise<void>` Gateway handler return; it rejects the test promise on handler failure and does not swallow production errors.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** Addressed by adding optional `title` and `toolCallId` to `ExecApprovalRequestParamsSchema` instead of keeping a parser-only mapping.
- **RF-002:** Addressed by adding after-fix proof from an actual Gateway-produced `exec.approval.requested` event passed into the ACP translator and resolved through the Gateway handler.
- **RF-003:** Addressed by extending `src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts` so translator-level coverage starts from the structured event shape and verifies ACP `request_permission` metadata.
- **RF-004:** Addressed by replacing helper-only proof with Gateway handler → broadcast payload → ACP translator → Gateway resolve proof.
- **RF-005:** Addressed by removing the test-only contract risk: the schema, producer, stored payload type, event broadcast, and translator coverage now agree on the optional metadata fields.
- **RF-006:** Addressed by defining the approval-boundary contract and sanitizing `title` with the existing exec approval display sanitizer before storing/broadcasting it; `toolCallId` is normalized as a non-empty optional string.
- **RF-007:** Addressed by implementing the recommended contract-backed option. Maintainer review is still expected for the public approval-boundary decision, but the branch no longer leaves the decision implicit in a parser-only patch.
- **RF-008:** Addressed by backing `src/acp/permission-relay.ts` metadata reads with a real Gateway schema/producer source.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts` for the Gateway-produced event → ACP translator proof.
- **Additional target test files:** `src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts` for schema/producer coverage and `src/acp/permission-relay.test.ts` for parser helper coverage.
- **Scenario locked in:** Gateway `exec.approval.request` accepts `title` and `toolCallId`, broadcasts them in `exec.approval.requested`, ACP uses those values in `request_permission`, and ACP decision resolution still targets the same Gateway approval id.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The tests cover the protocol schema, Gateway producer, structured event payload, ACP translator intake, and existing parser helper without launching unrelated channel transports.
- `pnpm vitest run src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts`
- `pnpm vitest run src/acp/permission-relay.test.ts`
- `pnpm check:test-types`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/exec-approvals.ts src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-request.ts src/gateway/server-methods/exec-approval.ts src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: 🚨 other` from the parser-only contract drift review.
- **Risk explanation:** This path crosses the exec approval display/permission boundary, so user-facing strings must be schema-backed and sanitized before ACP consumes them.
- **Why acceptable:** The metadata is optional, the existing fallback behavior remains for events that omit it, `title` uses the existing exec approval display sanitizer, `toolCallId` is only accepted as a normalized non-empty string, and approval decision semantics are unchanged. Compatibility risk is limited to adding optional schema fields, availability risk is covered by preserving request registration/resolution behavior, and security-boundary risk is covered by sanitizing display text before ACP consumes it.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low-to-moderate because this adds optional metadata to a public Gateway approval request/event contract. Existing clients that omit `title` or `toolCallId` keep the current fallback behavior, and the closed schema still rejects unrelated extra fields.

The stored approval request payload gains two optional fields only; command text, command preview, command argv, approval visibility, allowed decisions, and resolution behavior are unchanged.

## What was not changed

- Did not change ACP permission option mapping or Gateway approval decision policy.
- Did not change command hydration through `exec.approval.get`.
- Did not change legacy agent approval event parsing.
- Did not add third-party channel, Discord, or hosted provider behavior.
- Did not claim remote CI or external live proof before the updated PR checks run.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** `parseGatewayExecApprovalRequestEventPayload` was updated to read `request.title` and `request.toolCallId`, but the Gateway approval request schema and producer did not define or emit those fields, so real structured `exec.approval.requested` events could not satisfy the ACP parser contract.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The metadata is now introduced at the Gateway request contract and producer, stored in the pending approval payload, broadcast through the existing `buildRequestedApprovalEvent(record)` path, and then consumed by ACP. That fixes the source-of-truth event path rather than adding downstream fallback logic.
