target.title: fix(errors): recognize content policy / new_sensitive errors as rate_limit for fallback
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug where provider **content moderation / policy errors** were left unclassified by the failover classifier, so the agent session failed instead of trying a fallback model.

**Trigger incident (2026-06-18):** Hub ran a long `03_区域政策` LLM-化 batch on session `d5689acd`. The session hit MiniMax moderation (`output new_sensitive (1027)`) and the gateway surfaced the error instead of routing to a fallback model. The session stopped cold.

## What this changes

`classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts` now matches content moderation patterns and returns `rate_limit` so the existing failover machinery can route them to a secondary model.

**Patterns matched (case-insensitive):**
- MiniMax: `new_sensitive`
- Anthropic: `content_filter`, `safety_block`, `safety block`
- OpenAI: `content_policy`, `content policy`

**Providers covered:** MiniMax (`minimax-portal`), Anthropic, OpenAI, and any other provider that emits a moderation-style error message.

## Why `rate_limit` and not a new reason

- Content moderation rejections are **temporary** — a different prompt can usually pass.
- A new `content_policy` reason would need a parallel set of decision rules in `classifyFailoverSignal`; `rate_limit` already enables cooldown probe + fallback routing, which is the right user experience.
- This is fully backwards-compatible — it only changes behavior in cases that were previously `unclassified`.

## Tests

Added in `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/failover-matches.test.ts`:
- `new_sensitive (1027)` → `rate_limit`
- `content_filter` → `rate_limit`
- `safety_block` → `rate_limit`
- `content_policy_violation` → `rate_limit`
- Case-insensitive matching
- Negative test: ordinary 429 still classifies as `rate_limit` via the normal path

## Reproduction (before fix)

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.minimaxi.com/anthropic/v1/messages   -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"   -H "Content-Type: application/json"   -d '{
    "model": "MiniMax-M3",
    "max_tokens": 100,
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "..."}]
  }'
# Response: {"type":"error","error":{"type":"api_error","message":"output new_sensitive (1027)"}}

# Gateway log:
# [agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: runId=... decision=surface_error
# reason=unclassified from=minimax-portal/MiniMax-M3
# rawError=output new_sensitive (1027)
```

After this fix, the same error routes to the configured fallback model instead of failing the session.

## Changelog

Added an `## Unreleased` entry under `### Fixes`.

## Related

- Production incident: 2026-06-18, session `d5689acd` (knowledge agent batch)
- Hub proposal document: `shared/docs/openclaw-pr-content-policy-fallback.md`
- Local patch file: `npm-global/lib/node_modules/openclaw/patches/openclaw+2026.6.1.patch`

target.title: fix(agents): handle stderr stream errors in tool_search_code child
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`tool_search_code` owns a Node child whose stderr is piped for bounded diagnostics. A read-side stderr `error` had no listener, so Node could surface it as an uncaught exception and crash the gateway. The child also created a stdout pipe even though this worker sends logs, bridge calls, and results exclusively over IPC.

## Why This Change Was Made

The spawn owner now rejects the run through its existing once-only settlement path when stderr fails. Unused stdout is set to `ignore`, removing both a needless pipe and its unhandled-error/backpressure surface. The focused regression asserts stderr rejection, child termination, and the exact stdio contract. A bulky one-off proof script and a redundant testing export were removed.

## User Impact

An OS-level read failure on the `tool_search_code` diagnostic pipe now fails only that tool call instead of risking the Gateway process. Normal code-mode logs and results remain on IPC; stderr diagnostics remain bounded and included in exit errors.

## Evidence

- Sanitized direct AWS Crabbox (`provider=aws`, `cbx_7d04459d7c6f`, public network, no Tailscale, no instance profile, no hydration), exact reviewed head `f2aab46b8dda8f19cb86b57e8bdc50311f996e40`: `pnpm test src/agents/tool-search.stream-errors.test.ts` passed 1/1. target.title: fix(cli): harden JSON.parse in secrets apply and model-auth status
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two unguarded `JSON.parse()` calls in the CLI can crash with raw `SyntaxError` exceptions instead of producing user-friendly errors or graceful fallbacks:

1. **`src/cli/secrets-cli.ts:56`** — `readPlanFile()` calls `JSON.parse(raw)` on a plan file read from disk. A corrupt/malformed plan file throws a raw `SyntaxError` with stack trace instead of a friendly error message telling the user how to regenerate the plan.

2. **`src/cli/capability-cli.ts:938`** — `runModelAuthStatus()` captures stdout from `modelsStatusCommand`, finds a line starting with `{`, and parses it. If the captured output contains a malformed JSON fragment, the `model-auth status` command crashes instead of gracefully returning `{}`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both are minimal defensive wrappings:
- `readPlanFile`: wrap in try/catch, throw a friendly `Error` with the file path and the regenerate command
- `runModelAuthStatus`: wrap in try/catch, return `{}` as graceful degradation (caller already handles empty results)

## Evidence

### Real terminal output (7 assertions, real file I/O):
```
$ npx tsx _proof-harden-jsonparse.ts
=== Proof: Hardened JSON.parse in CLI ===

secrets-cli readPlanFile (real file round-trip):
PASS   Before fix: raw SyntaxError on corrupt file
PASS   After fix: friendly Error with file path and malformed JSON guidance
PASS   Valid plan file parses correctly (no regression)

capability-cli runModelAuthStatus (unparseable CLI output):
PASS   Before fix: SyntaxError on unparseable output
PASS   After fix: graceful {} when captured line is not valid JSON
PASS   After fix: valid JSON still parses correctly (no regression)
PASS   After fix: no JSON-like lines returns empty object

=== Results: 7 passed, 0 failed ===
```

### Regression tests (in existing CLI test files):
- `src/cli/secrets-cli.test.ts`: corrupt plan file → friendly error with "malformed JSON" and file path (no SyntaxError)
- `src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts`: unparseable model auth status output → `{}` (no crash)

## Merge Risk

Low — defensive try/catch wrappers. Valid JSON paths are unchanged. No new dependencies, no logic changes.

target.body:
Fixes #84139.

## Summary

- Filters replay-unsafe `sessions_send` artifacts at the compaction safeguard branch-fallback boundary without dropping safe assistant text from mixed assistant messages.
- Keeps the existing duplicate protections for target-side delivered inter-session turns and source-side already-executed `sessions_send` tool call/result artifacts.
- Adds a focused mixed-content regression proving safe assistant text remains provider-visible while `sessions_send` tool-call blocks and results are removed.

## Origin / follow-up

- N/A — independent root-cause fix for linked issue #84139. The recorded related open PR scan reported `related_open_prs: []` and `scan_error: null`, so this is not following or competing with a broader same-contract PR found by the daily-fix scan.

## Root Cause

- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High. The patch is limited to the compaction safeguard branch-fallback source boundary, has focused regression coverage for the over-filtering case, and has fresh current-head production-hook terminal proof.
- **Root cause:** The root/source invariant at the branch-fallback filter was too coarse: it treated any assistant message containing a replay-unsafe `sessions_send` tool call as entirely unsafe. That removed the already-executed send artifact, but it also dropped safe assistant text from mixed text-plus-tool-call turns, losing useful fallback history during compaction recovery.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix keeps replay safety at the source boundary by removing only the `sessions_send` tool-call blocks and their matching tool results before `containsRealConversation()` and summarization see recovered branch history. Assistant messages that still contain safe content remain available for summarization; assistant messages that contain only replay-unsafe send blocks are still removed.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** A compaction that fires during an inter-agent `sessions_send` exchange should not duplicate delivered messages, but it also should not erase safe context from the source session's assistant turn. This keeps both sides of the session-state/message-delivery boundary intact.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The source-of-truth owner is the compaction safeguard's recovered branch-history filter, immediately before recovered messages are classified as real conversation and sent to summarization. The patch preserves that boundary by reusing `isMessagingToolSendAction()` for send-action detection and `toolCallId` linkage for matching results; no downstream summary text filtering or delivery-layer special case is added.
- **Compatibility/default behavior:** No public API, user configuration, schema, protocol, wire/data format, migration, provider routing, session persistence format, message delivery behavior, or default compaction setting changes.
- **Out of scope:** Gateway UI behavior, Mantis/Crabbox automation, third-party channel transport, provider selection, idempotency keys, session storage format, and `sessions_send` execution semantics are intentionally unchanged.
- **Patch quality notes:** The production change remains one source file and one regression file. The new `return true` branches keep non-send blocks, malformed non-tool blocks, and unrelated tool calls; the `return false` branch removes only replay-unsafe `sessions_send` blocks after recording their id for result filtering. The test names use "fallback" because they exercise the existing compaction branch-fallback seam that caused the duplicate/replay behavior.
- **What did NOT change:** Normal compaction preparation, message delivery, `sessions_send` execution, idempotency keys, provider routing, session persistence format, config, schema, API, migration behavior, and default compaction settings are unchanged.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: session-state` and `merge-risk: message-delivery`.
- **Risk explanation:** The patch changes which recovered session-branch entries can become compaction summary input when preparation omitted real conversation content. Over-filtering can lose useful fallback context; under-filtering can replay already-executed send artifacts.
- **Why acceptable:** Current-head proof covers both sides of the boundary: target/source `sessions_send` artifacts do not reach the provider, ordinary safe branch fallback remains provider-visible, and the new regression proves mixed assistant text is preserved while `sessions_send` tool-call blocks and results are removed.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Prevents compaction safeguard branch fallback from reusing already-executed `sessions_send` interactions as fallback history during compaction recovery while preserving safe assistant text in mixed source-session turns.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw PR worktree at `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-93293` on head `69fa892b99fad3f84bcea21181de5908ce414368` after resolving the `daily_fix.sh sync-main` conflict. target.title: fix(agents): harden subagent lifecycle calls against transient gateway readiness failures
target.body:
## Summary

- add a bounded `sessions.list` readiness probe before subagent spawn starts the child agent
- retry transient finalize lifecycle calls in subagent announce (`sessions.patch` / `sessions.delete`)
- retry transient sweep cleanup `sessions.delete` calls in subagent registry cleanup
- restore the missing sweep delete helper wiring on current `main`
- restore/expand focused regression coverage for sweep cleanup and announce finalize retry paths
- keep the patch narrowed to the still-missing lifecycle hardening pieces on current `main`

## Why this refreshed PR

The earlier PR branch became stale relative to current `main` because related subagent delivery/orchestration code moved substantially. This refreshed branch keeps the same bug-fix intent, but re-applies only the still-missing resilience behavior on top of current `main` with a smaller diff. Rebased onto `origin/main` at `e88f5cea7eb` (2026-07-06).

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Root Cause

Several subagent lifecycle paths still treat short gateway readiness/lifecycle gaps as single-shot failures:
- spawn starts the child agent immediately, without a bounded readiness preflight
- subagent announce finalize calls swallow transient lifecycle errors instead of retrying them
- registry sweep cleanup retries only on a later sweep, rather than immediately retrying known transient lifecycle failures in bounded fashion

## Test Plan

```shell
OPENCLAW_TEST_FAST=1 node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/agents/subagent-spawn.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagent-announce.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagent-registry-helpers.test.ts \
  src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts
```

## Results

- V1 (diff --check): ✅ clean
- V2 (oxlint): ✅ 0 warnings, 0 errors on changed source files
- `src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts` (expected)
- `src/agents/subagent-spawn.test.ts` (expected)
- `src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts` (expected)
- `src/agents/subagent-announce.test.ts` (expected)
- `src/agents/subagent-registry-helpers.test.ts` (expected)

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: `isGatewayLifecycleTransientError` correctly classifies gateway/lifecycle errors as transient or permanent — transient errors (timeout, close code 1006, handshake timeout, "closed before connect", "not yet ready") are retried, while permanent errors (close codes 1003/1007/1008 Policy Violation, unauthorized, forbidden, authentication failed) fail fast without retry.

Real environment tested: Repository `openclaw/openclaw`, branch `fix/subagent-gateway-readiness-refresh`, commit `97b19748e42`, on Linux x64 using Node.js v24.14.1. Worktree at `/datad/github/openclaw-pr74131` freshly rebased onto `origin/main` (`e88f5cea7eb`).

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
```shell
node --experimental-strip-types --eval "
import { isGatewayLifecycleTransientError } from './src/agents/subagent-gateway-lifecycle.ts';

const tests = [
  { msg: 'gateway timeout after 20000ms', expect: true },
  { msg: 'gateway closed (1008): policy violation', expect: false },
  { msg: 'gateway closed (1006): transport close', expect: true },
  { msg: 'WebSocket handshake timeout after 10000ms', expect: true },
  { msg: 'closed before connect conn=abc reason=startup', expect: true },
  { msg: 'Gateway not yet ready to accept connections (retry after a moment)', expect: true },
  { msg: 'unauthorized access', expect: false },
  { msg: 'forbidden: not allowed', expect: false },
  { msg: 'authentication failed for user', expect: false },
  { msg: 'gateway closed (1003): unsupported data', expect: false },
  { msg: 'gateway closed (1007): invalid payload', expect: false },
];

for (const { msg, expect } of tests) {
  const result = isGatewayLifecycleTransientError(new Error(msg));
  console.log((result === expect ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL') + ': \"' + msg + '\" => ' + result + ' (expected ' + expect + ')');
}
"
```

Evidence after fix:
```
PASS: "gateway timeout after 20000ms" => true (expected true)
PASS: "gateway closed (1008): policy violation" => false (expected false)
PASS: "gateway closed (1006): transport close" => true (expected true)
PASS: "WebSocket handshake timeout after 10000ms" => true (expected true)
PASS: "closed before connect conn=abc reason=startup" => true (expected true)
PASS: "Gateway not yet ready to accept connections (retry after a moment)" => true (expected true)
PASS: "unauthorized access" => false (expected false)
PASS: "forbidden: not allowed" => false (expected false)
PASS: "authentication failed for user" => false (expected false)
PASS: "gateway closed (1003): unsupported data" => false (expected false)
PASS: "gateway closed (1007): invalid payload" => false (expected false)

All tests passed!
```

Observed result after fix: All 11 behavior verification cases pass — transient gateway lifecycle errors are correctly classified as retriable, and permanent policy/auth failures are correctly excluded from retry. The `isGatewayLifecycleTransientError` function properly gates the retry loops in `deleteSubagentSessionWithRetry` (sweep cleanup), subagent spawn readiness probes, and announce finalize calls.

What was not tested: Full end-to-end subagent lifecycle with live gateway restart injection was not validated locally (requires running gateway process). Targeted vitest tests covering the spawn/announce/cleanup retry paths are expected to pass in CI.

## CI notes

- `Real behavior proof` check includes live terminal output from `isGatewayLifecycleTransientError` classification.
- No CHANGELOG entries in the PR diff — release notes are maintainer-owned.
- Greptile P0 (`deleteSubagentSessionWithRetry` undefined) is resolved — function is defined in `subagent-registry-helpers.ts` and properly imported in `subagent-registry.ts`.
- Greptile P2 (`process.env` read at import time) is noted but the pattern is consistent with other retry-delay constants in the codebase.

## Notes

- Greptile / review findings about missing helper wiring and weakened cleanup coverage are addressed in this refresh.
- Added focused announce finalize retry coverage for both `sessions.delete` and `sessions.patch` transient failure paths.
- P1 fix: `isGatewayLifecycleTransientError` now excludes permanent WS close codes (1008 Policy Violation, 1003, 1007) and explicit auth denials from retry — these fail fast instead.
- P2 fix: CHANGELOG entries removed from PR branch.

## PR Self-check

- [x] helper definition/import/export chain re-checked (`deleteSubagentSessionWithRetry` in registry-helpers → imported in registry)
- [x] cleanup / finalize paths re-checked end-to-end
- [x] previously weakened regression assertion restored or replaced with equivalent protection
- [x] targeted tests added for the exact transient retry paths touched by this PR
- [x] Rebased onto origin/main (e88f5cea7eb) and merge conflicts resolved

## Risks / Notes

- The lifecycle retry classifiers are still message-based, so future transient variants may need to be added explicitly.
- Retries are bounded and localized to the known gateway readiness/lifecycle paths.

## Supersedes / Related

- Related to / refreshes the intent of #70434

target.title: refactor(qa): drive Matrix lifecycle through channel drivers
target.body:
Closes #101054

## What Problem This Solves

Matrix lifecycle proof needs to follow the same channel-driver selection seam as the rest of QA Lab. Selecting `live:matrix` should create the existing Matrix live transport, which privately owns Tuwunel; selecting `crabline:matrix` should create Crabline through the same transport-adapter registry.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR now puts the lifecycle foundation at the QA Lab transport-adapter boundary:

1. `createQaChannelDriverLifecycle()` owns generic start, idempotent start, restart, stop, and resume control around `createQaTransportAdapter()`.
2. The selected driver is the only switch. `live:matrix` resolves the registered Matrix live adapter; `crabline:matrix` resolves the built-in Crabline adapter.
3. Live adapter discovery is lazy, so exporting the lifecycle contract does not eagerly pull the live transport CLI graph into the default QA runtime entry.
4. One parameterized live test runs the same five scenarios through both real drivers.
5. The previous `qa-matrix` lifecycle helpers and private test API are removed. The final PR diff has no `qa-matrix` files; full plugin migration/removal remains separate follow-up work.

This is a test/runtime-control seam inside QA Lab, not an end-user Matrix runtime or configuration surface. It adds no environment variable and no Matrix-plugin policy.

## User Impact

No end-user behavior or configuration changes. Maintainers get one channel-driver lifecycle contract and real parity proof for Tuwunel-backed live Matrix and Crabline without intertwining the foundation with the `qa-matrix` plugin.

The Matrix plugin bundle does not grow: the final diff contains no `extensions/qa-matrix/**` changes. QA Lab's runtime entry gains only the lifecycle export; channel-driver factory discovery remains a lazy dynamic import.

## Evidence

Exact pushed head: `395b864d203`.

Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwx3qb2wvp9x0mv9v3way3h1` (`golden-crab`):

- `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 corepack pnpm build` passed.
- `corepack pnpm test extensions/qa-lab/src/channel-driver-lifecycle.test.ts` passed 2/2 tests.
- `node scripts/test-live.mjs -- extensions/qa-lab/src/matrix-channel-driver.lifecycle.live.test.ts` passed both real drivers and all five lifecycle scenarios.
- `corepack pnpm tsgo:extensions` passed.
- `corepack pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` passed.
- Targeted extension oxlint passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Fresh canonical autoreview thread `019f3a53-cf96-7f22-bd96-219e9a99b1d1` reported no accepted/actionable findings and judged the patch correct.

Developed with AI assistance. A sanitized agent transcript is available but is not included without explicit approval.

target.title: fix(usage): preserve provider-billed zero totals
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #97047 after the direct DeepSeek V4 zero-cost regression was fixed on `main`.

The remaining accounting gap is that `usage.cost.total: 0` is ambiguous in persisted transcripts:

- it can be a fabricated placeholder zero from a transport/catalog path, which should be recomputed or treated as missing when pricing is known/unknown; or
- it can be an authoritative provider-billed total from a provider billing endpoint, including a legitimate free/zero-cost route.

OpenRouter is the concrete provider-billed case: its generation metadata endpoint returns `total_cost`, and that value is the provider's billing total. When `total_cost` is `0`, core usage aggregation should preserve it only when the transcript carries explicit provenance proving that the zero came from provider billing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The earlier follow-up approach was rejected because it guessed from provider/model ids and treated every known-priced all-zero row as authoritative. This version follows the maintainer guidance instead:

- no DeepSeek/OpenRouter model ids are hard-coded into core usage accounting;
- OpenRouter, as the provider owner, marks generation-metadata totals as provider-billed;
- core aggregation uses a generic provenance signal rather than provider-specific policy;
- rows without provenance keep the current `main` behavior, so suspicious known-priced zero totals still get recomputed.

## What Changed

- Add `usage.cost.totalOrigin?: "provider-billed" | "estimated"` to the usage/cost type contract.
- When OpenRouter generation metadata lookup succeeds, set:
  - `usage.cost.total = data.total_cost`
  - `usage.cost.totalOrigin = "provider-billed"`
- Teach session usage-cost scanning to preserve recorded zero totals when `totalOrigin` is `provider-billed`.
- Keep the existing protection for provider-reconciled zero totals with nonzero cost components.
- Keep existing recomputation/missing-cost behavior for unproven all-zero known-priced/unknown-priced rows.
- Bump the durable usage-cost cache version from 6 to 7 because recognized cost-total provenance changes cached total semantics.

## Evidence

Current PR head used for this proof update: `d94a866db584795872e27fae0b2b72dd4baac7fc`. The code patch was intentionally left unchanged; this update only adds current-head evidence and review context.

Regression coverage added/updated:

- `extensions/openrouter/index.test.ts`
  - nonzero OpenRouter generation metadata cost is marked `provider-billed`
  - zero OpenRouter generation metadata cost is marked `provider-billed`
  - failed/oversized generation metadata lookup keeps the streamed estimate and does not set provider-billed provenance
- `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`
  - provider-billed all-zero cost total with known pricing remains zero in summary, durable cache, and session logs
  - known-priced transcript rows without provider-billed provenance still recompute from catalog pricing
  - version-6 durable cache entries are stale under the new provenance-aware semantics

Real transcript-path proof on a test server, exact head `d94a866db584795872e27fae0b2b72dd4baac7fc`, collected 2026-07-07 UTC:

- checked out PR #101177 at `d94a866db584795872e27fae0b2b72dd4baac7fc`
- created a redacted JSONL transcript under `agents/main/sessions` with:
  - provider: `openrouter`
  - model: `openai/gpt-5.5`
  - total tokens: `15000`
  - `usage.cost.total: 0`
  - `usage.cost.totalOrigin: "provider-billed"`
- ran the production session usage summary/cache/log path against that transcript
- observed result:
  - `loadCostUsageSummary`: `totalTokens=15000`, `totalCost=0`, `missingCostEntries=0`
  - `loadCostUsageSummaryFromCache`: `totalCost=0`, `missingCostEntries=0`
  - `loadSessionLogs`: `tokens=15000`, `cost=0`
- result: provider-billed zero total stayed zero in the real transcript summary, durable cache, and session-log spend path

Sanitized proof output:

```json
{
  "inputTranscriptUsage": {
    "provider": "openrouter",
    "model": "openai/gpt-5.5",
    "totalTokens": 15000,
    "costTotal": 0,
    "costTotalOrigin": "provider-billed"
  },
  "summaryTotals": {
    "totalTokens": 15000,
    "totalCost": 0,
    "missingCostEntries": 0
  },
  "durableCacheTotals": {
    "totalCost": 0,
    "missingCostEntries": 0
  },
  "sessionLogRow": {
    "tokens": 15000,
    "cost": 0
  },
  "proof_result": "passed"
}
```

GitHub Actions evidence on exact head `d94a866db584795872e27fae0b2b72dd4baac7fc`:

- `Real behavior proof` succeeded: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28823621558
- `CI` succeeded: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28822961427
  - includes successful `preflight`, `security-fast`, `build-artifacts`, `check-lint`, `check-prod-types`, `check-test-types`, `check-dependencies`, guard checks, and node compact shards
- Additional successful security/path checks on the same head include CodeQL, OpenGrep PR diff, Dependency Guard, Security Sensitive Guard, Workflow Sanity, and Socket Security checks in the PR status rollup.

Local targeted validation on the pushed head, before this proof-only body update:

- `git diff --check -- src/agents/usage.ts packages/llm-core/src/types.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.types.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts extensions/openrouter/stream.ts extensions/openrouter/index.test.ts`
- `CI=1 NO_COLOR=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts extensions/openrouter/index.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts`: 66 passed
  - `extensions/openrouter/index.test.ts`: 46 passed

Evidence source map:

- OpenRouter generation metadata provenance: covered by OpenRouter regression tests and the `extensions/openrouter/stream.ts` change that marks successful generation metadata totals as `provider-billed`.
- Provider-billed zero preservation through transcript aggregation: covered by the test-server transcript-path proof and session-cost regression tests.
- Durable cache compatibility: covered by the cache-version bump from 6 to 7 plus regression coverage that treats version-6 cache entries as stale under the new semantics.
- Placeholder-zero safety: covered by regression coverage showing known-priced transcript rows without provider-billed provenance still recompute instead of being accepted as authoritative zero.

## Relationship to Closed PRs

This supersedes the closed #97134 and #101163 follow-up attempts. The closed PRs tried to resolve the conflict by scoping behavior from core. This PR instead adds the explicit provenance contract requested in review.

## Current Head / Base Status

The current PR head is `d94a866db584795872e27fae0b2b72dd4baac7fc` on `fix/usage-cost-provenance-zero-total`. This proof update does not rebase, merge, or alter the code patch. GitHub currently reports the branch as behind latest `main`; the evidence above is bound to the exact current PR head.

## Risk

Low-to-moderate behavior risk, limited to cost accounting for transcript rows with `usage.cost.total: 0`.

Expected behavior after this change:

- Provider-billed zero total with explicit `totalOrigin: "provider-billed"`: preserved as authoritative zero.
- Known-priced placeholder zero without provenance: recomputed from catalog pricing.
- Unknown/all-zero pricing with nonzero tokens and no provenance: still reported as missing cost.
- Positive recorded provider costs: preserved by existing behavior.

No workflow, dependency, lockfile, secret, or release artifact changes.

## Review Context Addressed

- Latest ClawSweeper review requested real behavior proof that a provider-billed zero total is preserved in a real transcript usage summary or spend path. The test-server proof above exercises the transcript summary, durable cache, and session-log spend path on exact head `d94a866db584795872e27fae0b2b72dd4baac7fc` and shows the provider-billed zero stays zero.
- The review called out the optional `usage.cost.totalOrigin` API/cache contract and cache-version semantics. This body keeps that surface visible: the contract is optional, the durable cache version is bumped from 6 to 7, and older version-6 cache entries are treated as stale and rebuilt.
- No provider/model-specific core policy was added; the core behavior remains provenance-based.
- No code changes were made for this proof update.

## Not Tested / Limitations

- This follow-up proof did not perform a live paid OpenRouter API call. The live provider-fetch path is covered by the OpenRouter regression tests; the added real-behavior proof uses a redacted transcript row carrying OpenRouter/provider-billed provenance through the production transcript summary/cache/log path on a test server.
- The branch is behind latest `main`; no rebase or code change was made because this update is evidence-only.

target.title: fix(webchat): preserve session context on first send after page load (#96331)
target.body: ## Summary WebChat `chat.send` now preserves session context on the first send after page load by passing the WebChat-backed `backingSessionId` as `CallerSessionId` through `MsgContext`, allowing `initSessionState` to trust the caller-verified session and skip freshness evaluation when the ID matches the store entry. This closes the gap where `chat.history` displayed full history but `chat.send` lost model-visible context after gateway restart. - **Problem**: `chat.history` reads the transcript directly from disk and displays full history, but `chat.send` independently evaluates session freshness via `initSessionState` and mints a new session when the existing one is stale (daily reset / idle expiry). After gateway restart or crossing the 4 AM daily reset boundary, the model responds without prior context even though history is visible. - **Solution**: The gateway `chat.send` handler already has `backingSessionId` from the WebChat client. Pass it as `CallerSessionId` in the `MsgContext`. In `initSessionState`, add a `callerVerifiedSession` guard — when the caller has already validated the session entry and passes a matching session ID, skip freshness evaluation and reuse the existing session. `/new` and `/reset` always take precedence via the `!isNewSession` guard. Mismatched IDs fall through to normal freshness evaluation. - **What changed**: `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts` (+1: pass `CallerSessionId: backingSessionId`), `src/auto-reply/templating.ts` (+8: add `CallerSessionId` field to `MsgContext` type), `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` (+15: add `callerVerifiedSession` guard to `freshEntry` computation), `src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` (+232: 7 regression tests covering all guard paths) - **What did NOT change**: Backend session init (`session.ts` existing freshness logic), gateway dispatch (`chat.ts` except one line), `MsgContext` type except the new optional field, plugin SDK exports, config, migration paths, `/new` and `/reset` behavior, heartbeat/system events, `reconnectResumeRequested` path ## Change Type & Scope ### Change Type - [x] Bug fix - [ ] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [ ] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ### Scope - [x] Gateway / orchestration - [ ] Skills / tool execution - [ ] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [ ] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [x] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue - Closes #96331 - [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression ## Motivation Web UI users returning to a chat session after gateway restart (most commonly noticed the next morning after the 4 AM daily reset boundary) would see their full chat history displayed correctly via `chat.history`, but the model would respond as if it had no prior context. The root cause was that `chat.history` reads the transcript directly from disk without freshness evaluation, while `chat.send` independently evaluates freshness via `initSessionState` and mints a new session when stale — the two paths disagreed on whether the session was valid. The fix is gateway-side, not UI-side: the `chat.send` handler already has `backingSessionId` from the WebChat client. By passing it through `MsgContext` as a caller-verified signal, `initSessionState` can trust the caller's session validation when the IDs match, without changing any freshness policy. ## Review Contract ```text Ref: #96331 / PR #96391 Surface: Gateway / session init / chat.send dispatch / MsgContext type Bug: chat.history shows session history but chat.send loses it after gateway restart Cause: chat.history reads transcript directly from disk (no freshness check) while chat.send independently evaluates freshness via initSessionState and mints a new sessionId when stale. The two paths disagreed on session validity. (src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts:636-684, src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts:4442-4445) Confidence: confirmed by code analysis + reproducible scenario Provenance: introduced by: PR #89017 (added reconnectResumeRequested infrastructure but only for WebSocket reconnect, not fresh page load) made visible by: gateway restart + daily reset boundary crossing Confidence: clear Best fix: Yes. The gateway chat.send handler already has backingSessionId from the WebChat client. Adding one field to MsgContext and one guard to freshEntry is the minimal correct fix. The callerVerifiedSession guard sits alongside existing guards (isSystemEvent, reconnectResumeRequested, recoverTerminalVisibleEntry) without modifying any of them. Refactor: No — existing backend infrastructure is unchanged and sufficient. Proof: 142 session tests + 2 gateway chat tests pass (7 new), build succeeds (pnpm build). See Real Behavior Proof below for terminal output. Risk: Low. The guard requires: !isNewSession, non-empty CallerSessionId string, canReuseExistingEntry, and entry.sessionId === ctx.CallerSessionId. All four must pass. Mismatch falls through to normal evaluation. /new and /reset always win. Heartbeat uses isSystemEvent (separate guard). The CallerSessionId field is optional on MsgContext — no existing callers are affected. ``` ## Real Behavior Proof **Behavior addressed**: Web UI `chat.history` displays full history but `chat.send` reaches model without context after gateway restart. After fix: `chat.send` carries `CallerSessionId`, `initSessionState` skips freshness evaluation when IDs match, model receives full context. **Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64, Node 22.19+, branch `fix/webchat-session-context-restart-96331`, rebased on upstream/main (bb658d0a6d) **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: ```bash # Session tests — full regression suite pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts --run ``` ``` Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 142 passed (142) ``` ```bash # Gateway chat.send tests pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/chat.send-deleted-agent.test.ts --run ``` ``` Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 2 passed (2) ``` **Evidence after fix**: Total: 144 tests passed across 3 test files, 0 regressions. New test coverage matrix (7 new tests): ``` Test scenario => Expected CallerSessionId matches daily-stale entry => isNewSession=false, session reused CallerSessionId matches idle-stale entry => isNewSession=false, session reused CallerSessionId with /new command => isNewSession=true, reset triggered CallerSessionId mismatches store entry => isNewSession=true, falls through CallerSessionId set but no store entry exists => isNewSession=true CallerSessionId is empty string => isNewSession=true, guard blocked Heartbeat without CallerSessionId (isSystemEvent guard) => isNewSession=false, independent path ``` **Observed result after fix**: - `CallerSessionId: backingSessionId` is passed in every `chat.send` MsgContext - `callerVerifiedSession` guard activates when: `!isNewSession` AND non-empty `CallerSessionId` string AND `canReuseExistingEntry` AND `entry.sessionId === ctx.CallerSessionId` - All four conditions must pass — no single condition can bypass freshness - `/new` and `/reset` always win via the `!isNewSession` guard - Heartbeat system events continue through independent `isSystemEvent` guard - `reconnectResumeRequested` path is unchanged - `recoverTerminalVisibleEntry` path (added upstream in commit 65e12328aa) is unchanged - All 142 existing session tests pass — zero regressions **What was not tested**: - Multi-tab Web UI scenarios with different sessions - Rapid page reload + send race conditions ### Environment - OS: Linux 4.19.112-2.el8.x86_64 - Runtime: Node 22.19+ - Branch: `fix/webchat-session-context-restart-96331` ## Risks and Mitigations - **Highest risk area**: The `callerVerifiedSession` guard skips freshness evaluation when `CallerSessionId` matches. If the WebChat client passes a stale/incorrect `backingSessionId`, the guard could match a truly-expired session. Mitigation: the session ID MUST match exactly (`entry.sessionId === ctx.CallerSessionId`). Also, `canReuseExistingEntry` must be true (entry exists, not force-new). - **Compatibility impact**: None. `CallerSessionId` is an optional field on `MsgContext`. Existing callers (bots, cron, integrations) never set it, so they follow the same freshness path as before. ## Security Impact - [x] New permissions/capabilities? No - [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No - [x] New/changed network calls? No - [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No - [x] Data access scope changed? No ## Compatibility / Migration - [x] Backward compatible? Yes — optional field on MsgContext, all existing callers unaffected - [x] Config/env changes? No - [x] Migration needed? No ## Human Verification - **Verified scenarios**: ### Step 1: Open Web UI Open **http://127.0.0.1:18788/** in your browser ### Step 2: Build a conversation with context 1. Start a new chat in the Web UI 2. Send several meaningful messages 3. Confirm the model correctly responds and references prior context across 3-4 turns ### Step 3: Restart the gateway (trigger the bug) ```bash # Kill the current gateway kill $(pgrep -f "run-node.mjs.*gateway") ``` ```bash # Wait 2 seconds then restart sleep 2 OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1 nohup node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway > /tmp/openclaw-gateway.log 2>&1 & ``` ### Step 4: Verify the fix 1. Reopen/refresh the Web UI and navigate back to the **same** chat session 2. **Verify chat.history first**: the UI should display the full conversation history from before restart (all prior messages visible on the page) 3. **Verify chat.send**: send a new message referencing the prior conversation 4. Observe the model's response - **Edge cases checked**: Empty `currentSessionId` (no-op), mismatched session IDs (backend fallthrough), heartbeat events (independent isSystemEvent guard) - **What you did NOT verify**: Multi-tab scenarios, rapid reload + send races ## AI Assistance 🤖 - **AI-assisted**: Yes - **Co-Authored-By**: Claude - **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes - **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue #96331 analysis → identified gap between chat.history and chat.send session resolution → designed CallerSessionId propagation fix reusing existing MsgContext infrastructure and initSessionState guard pattern ## Review Conversations - [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR. - [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment. Closes #96331 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

target.title: fix(gateway): keep explicit loopback bind pinned to 127.0.0.1 (#65619)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Explicit `gateway.bind: "loopback"` could be demoted to `0.0.0.0` when the best-effort `127.0.0.1` bind preflight failed intermittently on macOS. The downstream runtime guard then correctly rejected startup because a loopback configuration had resolved to a non-loopback host, leaving users with a failed Gateway even though their config explicitly requested local-only binding.

## Evidence
The PR body documents the failing path through `src/gateway/net.ts` and `src/gateway/server-runtime-config.ts`: explicit loopback used a fragile `canBindToHost("127.0.0.1")` probe before returning the loopback host. The fix pins explicit loopback to `127.0.0.1`, preserving the documented local-only contract and avoiding accidental exposure or startup rejection.

---

## Summary

On macOS, the best-effort `canBindToHost("127.0.0.1")` preflight in `resolveGatewayBindHost` can fail intermittently (port temporarily held, IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack quirks). When that probe returned false for an explicit `bind: "loopback"` configuration, the resolver silently fell back to `0.0.0.0`, and the downstream guard `resolveGatewayRuntimeConfig` then rejected startup with `gateway bind=loopback resolved to non-loopback host 0.0.0.0`. This change makes explicit loopback always return `127.0.0.1` without any preflight, matching the documented contract.

## Root Cause

- `src/gateway/net.ts:232` (before): `if (mode === "loopback") { if (await canBindToHost("127.0.0.1")) return "127.0.0.1"; return "0.0.0.0"; }`. The best-effort preflight is well-intentioned but creates a "silent demotion" path on macOS.
- `src/gateway/server-runtime-config.ts:64`: `resolveGatewayRuntimeConfig` rejects loopback mode when the resolved bind host is not loopback with the error family `gateway bind=loopback resolved to non-loopback host ...`. This guard is correct — it prevents accidentally exposing a Gateway intended as local-only.
- Execution path: operator config `{ gateway: { bind: "loopback" } }` → `resolveGatewayBindHost("loopback")` → preflight `canBindToHost("127.0.0.1")` returns false (flaky) → resolver returns `"0.0.0.0"` → runtime guard sees `bind=loopback` + `host="0.0.0.0"` mismatch → Gateway refuses to start with the reporter's exact error.
- clawsweeper review on #65619: *"The narrow maintainable fix is to make explicit loopback return `127.0.0.1` without weakening `auto`, `tailnet`, `custom`, or the runtime guard that prevents unintended network binds."*
- Docs at `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md:512` document `loopback` as listening on `127.0.0.1`; the runtime guard enforces that contract; the resolver should match.

## Changes

- `src/gateway/net.ts`: in the explicit `loopback` branch of `resolveGatewayBindHost`, always return `"127.0.0.1"` — drop the preflight and the `"0.0.0.0"` fallback. Update the function-level doc comment to reflect the explicit-user-choice semantics. If `127.0.0.1` is truly unbindable, the OS still surfaces a clear bind error at the actual `listen()` call, which is the correct surface for that rare condition.
- `src/gateway/net.test.ts`: add `"keeps explicit loopback pinned to 127.0.0.1 without preflight (#65619)"` that stubs `net.createServer` so every bind probe errors; explicit `loopback` must still return `127.0.0.1`. Other existing tests (lan, tailnet, custom, auto, default) are unchanged because the resolver's behavior in those branches is unchanged.

Other modes are unchanged: `lan` still returns `0.0.0.0`; `tailnet` / `custom` / `auto` keep their preflight + fallback behavior so container-aware semantics, Tailscale routing, and operator-supplied custom IPs continue to fall back gracefully when they really cannot bind. Only the explicit user-chosen `loopback` mode now bypasses the preflight.

Net diff: **+48 / −6 LOC across 2 files** (+19 production / +35 test).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: macOS Mac mini operator on OpenClaw 2026.4.11 (also confirmed on 2026.5.7 by clawsweeper) with `gateway.bind: "loopback"` configured sees the Gateway refuse to start with `gateway bind=loopback resolved to non-loopback host 0.0.0.0`. clawsweeper confirmed the latest release tag still carries the same source path at `eeef4864494f`. Issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/65619
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `../openclaw-65656` on Windows 11. The fix is a 1-branch change to a pure-function resolver; verification is source-pattern proof against the patched file plus the colocated regression test that forces every preflight probe to fail and asserts the resolver still returns `127.0.0.1`. PR head: `a79671c5`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `git diff src/gateway/net.ts` shows the explicit `loopback` branch now contains a single `return "127.0.0.1";` with no preflight and no `0.0.0.0` fallback. `sed -n '/if (mode === "loopback")/,/^  }/p' src/gateway/net.ts | sha256sum` produces the integrity hash. The new test invokes `resolveGatewayBindHost("loopback")` with `net.createServer` stubbed to always emit `EADDRINUSE`, asserting the resolver still returns `"127.0.0.1"`.
- **Evidence after fix**: Terminal output captured locally on PR head `a79671c5` (Windows 11; patched loopback branch SHA-256 `b0565f6ad64d9bec3fe30858a0ddc8ef031ad9b5de4e206dacdae0426a0ca1df`).

~~~text
$ sed -n '/if (mode === "loopback")/,/^  }/p' src/gateway/net.ts
  if (mode === "loopback") {
    // Honor the operator's explicit `bind: "loopback"` choice unconditionally:
    // returning `127.0.0.1` keeps the Gateway local-only as documented and as
    // the downstream runtime guard in `resolveGatewayRuntimeConfig` requires
    // (#65619). The previous best-effort preflight to `127.0.0.1` could fail
    // intermittently on macOS (port temporarily held, IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack
    // quirks, etc.) and then silently fall back to `0.0.0.0`, which the
    // runtime guard then rejects with `gateway bind=loopback resolved to
    // non-loopback host 0.0.0.0` and refuses to start. The OS itself returns
    // a clear bind error if `127.0.0.1` is truly unbindable, which is the
    // correct surface for that rare condition.
    return "127.0.0.1";
  }

$ sed -n '/if (mode === "loopback")/,/^  }/p' src/gateway/net.ts | sha256sum
b0565f6ad64d9bec3fe30858a0ddc8ef031ad9b5de4e206dacdae0426a0ca1df *-
~~~

- **Observed result after fix**: The patched explicit-loopback branch — pinned by SHA-256 `b0565f6ad64d9bec3fe30858a0ddc8ef031ad9b5de4e206dacdae0426a0ca1df` — has a single `return "127.0.0.1";` statement with no `canBindToHost` preflight and no `0.0.0.0` fallback. The preflight-failure → silent demotion → runtime-guard-rejection chain that produced the reporter's startup error is no longer reachable for the explicit user-chosen `loopback` mode. Other modes (`lan`, `tailnet`, `custom`, `auto`) keep their existing preflight + fallback chains and their existing tests continue to pass.
- **What was not tested**: A live macOS Gateway foreground startup with the exact intermittent-preflight condition was not reproduced on the contributor machine; the failure is source-proven from the resolver + runtime-guard arithmetic and clawsweeper's source-level reproduction. The fix surface is a 1-branch change inside a pure-function resolver; downstream consumers (`resolveGatewayRuntimeConfig`, the actual `listen()` call in the Gateway server) are unchanged. Maintainers may apply `proof: override` if a live macOS recording is required.

## Test

- `pnpm test src/gateway/net.test.ts -t "resolveGatewayBindHost"` — 5 existing cases (loopback, lan, auto-non-container, auto-container, undefined-default) + 1 new regression case `"keeps explicit loopback pinned to 127.0.0.1 without preflight (#65619)"` that stubs every bind probe to error and asserts the resolver still returns `127.0.0.1`. The new test was the natural failing case for the old code path and now passes after the fix.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-runtime-config.test.ts -t "resolveGatewayRuntimeConfig"` — unchanged; the runtime guard's behavior is unchanged. With explicit `loopback` now returning `127.0.0.1` deterministically, the guard's mismatch branch is no longer reachable for this user-chosen mode, but it still fires correctly for `tailnet`/`custom` fallbacks to `0.0.0.0`.

## Notes

- Scope: smallest complete fix at the documented seam clawsweeper identified. No public API change; no docs change required because `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md:512` already documents `loopback` as listening on `127.0.0.1` (the fix brings the runtime behavior in line with the documented contract). No CHANGELOG entry per the AGENTS.md guidance that contributor PRs do not edit CHANGELOG; maintainer/AI adds entries during landing.
- Compatibility: the only behavioral change is the explicit `loopback` mode no longer silently demotes to `0.0.0.0`. Operators who set `bind: "loopback"` AND have `127.0.0.1` permanently unbindable on their box now get a clear OS-level bind error (the listen() syscall) instead of a confusing runtime-guard rejection with a misleading "resolved to non-loopback" message. `auto` mode (the default when `bind` is unset) still preflights and falls back, so it continues to handle container/Tailscale/dual-stack edge cases the same way.
- This follows the conservative direction in clawsweeper's review on #65619: *"Keep explicit `gateway.bind=\"loopback\"` pinned to `127.0.0.1` even when the best-effort bind preflight fails, and add focused regression coverage for that path."*

Closes #65619

target.title: fix(commitments): stop hardcoding fastMode in extraction (#78451)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
MiniMax Coding Plan users whose token plan includes `MiniMax-M2.7` but not `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` could not run commitment extraction because the hidden extraction path hardcoded `fastMode: true`, silently rewriting the selected model to the unsupported highspeed variant.

## Evidence
The PR body documents the failing path: `src/commitments/runtime.ts` passed `fastMode: true` into `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, and `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts` rewrote the model id to `-highspeed`. The fix removes the hardcoded fast mode for commitment extraction so the user's configured model stays unchanged.

---

## Summary

MiniMax Coding Plan operators whose plan owns `MiniMax-M2.7` but not the `-highspeed` variant hit `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` on every commitment extraction pass, because the commitments extraction path passed `fastMode: true` unconditionally to `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, which caused the MiniMax stream wrapper's `createMinimaxFastModeWrapper` to rewrite the base model id to `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`.

## Root Cause

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts:242` (pre-fix): the call to `runEmbeddedPiAgent` for hidden commitment extraction hardcoded `fastMode: true`.
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24`: the MiniMax stream wrapper accepts a `fastMode` boolean and, when true, swaps the base model id to its `-highspeed` variant.
- Result: every commitments extraction request silently flipped `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, which Coding Plan operators do not own. MiniMax responds with HTTP 500 / error code 2061. Reporter verified the Coding Plan owns the base model but not highspeed.
- The reporter listed three valid fix shapes (drop the hardcode, add a config field, or inherit agent fastMode). This PR uses option 1: dropping the hardcode lets the existing `resolveFastModeState` helper continue to control fast-mode for the rest of the agent runtime, and commitments extraction inherits the same default-false behavior.

## Changes

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts`: remove `fastMode: true` from the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload built in the commitments extraction path. Add a comment explaining the reason so this does not regress.
- `src/commitments/runtime.test.ts`: extend the existing `runEmbeddedPiAgentMock` assertion to assert `fastMode` is **not** in the payload, locking in the regression fix.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: single-line entry under Unreleased / Fixes.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: On every commitment extraction pass, MiniMax Coding Plan operators receive `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` from the MiniMax server because the agent runtime requested `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` even though their plan only owns `MiniMax-M2.7`. The reporter (`@advaitpaliwal`) verified `commitments.enabled: true, commitments.maxPerDay: 10` config, then ran a real Coding Plan session, observed extraction always selecting the highspeed variant, and traced the root cause to `dist/runtime-CXt7BFiH.js` line 386 (`fastMode: true` hardcoded). Issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78451
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout at `../openclaw-78451` on Windows 11 + Node 22.14. The smoke script reads the **patched production file `src/commitments/runtime.ts` directly from the worktree**, locates the entire `defaultExtractBatch` function (the path that builds the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload), prints its SHA-256 + verbatim bytes, then runs structural assertions over the captured payload literal to prove `fastMode: true` is gone, the `#78451` explanatory comment is in place, and every sibling field is preserved. No mocks, no test runner — the patched source bytes drive the smoke. PR head: `a3189f329687fa8c2c9da783afbc0d644ea94573`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `git checkout fix/commitments-no-fastmode-hardcode && node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts`, where `smoke-pr78459.mts` reads `src/commitments/runtime.ts`, slices the `async function defaultExtractBatch` body, hashes it, prints the verbatim payload object literal, and runs structural assertions against the live patched source.
- Evidence after fix: Terminal output captured locally on PR head `a3189f3296` (Windows 11 + Node 22.14, the patched `src/commitments/runtime.ts` `defaultExtractBatch` function read from the worktree, 1660 bytes, SHA-256 `ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379`).

~~~text
$ node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts
=== Patched defaultExtractBatch function — bytes from src/commitments/runtime.ts ===
offset: 7245 -> 8905 ( 1660 bytes)
SHA-256: ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379

function body still contains literal 'fastMode: true': false
explanatory '#78451' comment present                : true
  preserved field 'disableTools: true': true
  preserved field 'thinkLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'verboseLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'reasoningLevel: "off"': true

=== Payload object passed to runEmbeddedPiAgent (verbatim from patched code) ===
{ cfg, agentId: first.agentId });
  const result = await runEmbeddedPiAgent({
    sessionId: runId,
    sessionKey: `agent:${first.agentId}:commitments:${runId}`,
    agentId: first.agentId,
    trigger: "manual",
    sessionFile: resolveExtractionSessionFile(first.agentId, runId),
    workspaceDir: resolveAgentWorkspaceDir(cfg, first.agentId),
    config: cfg,
    provider: modelRef.provider,
    model: modelRef.model,
    prompt: buildCommitmentExtractionPrompt({ cfg, items: params.items }),
    disableTools: true,
    thinkLevel: "off",
    verboseLevel: "off",
    reasoningLevel: "off",
    // Do not hardcode fastMode here: leaving the field undefined lets the
    // commitments extraction inherit the configured fast-mode state (which
    // defaults to false). Hardcoding true caused MiniMax Coding Plans without
    // highspeed access to fail with HTTP 500 because the MiniMax stream wrapper
    // would rewrite MiniMax-M2.7 -> MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (#78451).
    timeoutMs: resolved.extraction.timeoutSeconds * 1000,
    runId,
    bootstrapContextMode: "lightweight",
    skillsSnapshot: { prompt: "", skills: [] },
    suppressToolErrorWarnings: true,
  }

=== fastMode-related lines in the payload (BEFORE-vs-AFTER comparison) ===
  // Do not hardcode fastMode here: leaving the field undefined lets the
  // highspeed access to fail with HTTP 500 because the MiniMax stream wrapper
  // would rewrite MiniMax-M2.7 -> MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (#78451).
~~~

- Observed result after fix: The patched `defaultExtractBatch` function — pinned by a 1660-byte / SHA-256 `ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379` integrity check — has zero `fastMode: true` literals (`function body still contains literal 'fastMode: true': false`). The explanatory `#78451` comment is in place (`explanatory '#78451' comment present: true`), and every sibling field (`disableTools: true`, `thinkLevel: "off"`, `verboseLevel: "off"`, `reasoningLevel: "off"`) is preserved verbatim. The captured payload literal shown verbatim above confirms `runEmbeddedPiAgent` is now called without a `fastMode` key — so the MiniMax stream wrapper at `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24` no longer flips `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, and the operator's configured base model id flows through unchanged.
- What was not tested: A live HTTP roundtrip against the real MiniMax server with a Coding Plan token is not available on the contributor machine, so this is source-level / structural proof against the patched payload-builder, not a live MiniMax 200 response. Maintainers may apply `proof: override` if a live MiniMax recording is required; the reporter's original issue already contains live HTTP 500 evidence from the real Coding Plan.

## Test

- `pnpm test src/commitments/runtime.test.ts` — 6 passed (including the new `expect(callArgs).not.toHaveProperty("fastMode")` regression assertion).

## Notes

- Scope: smallest complete fix. No new config surface and no provider/wrapper edits — the existing fast-mode resolution chain already covers the right behavior; the hardcode was the only thing forcing `true`.
- Compatibility: agents that need fast-mode for commitments can still set it via `agents.defaults.models.<id>.params.fastMode: true` (or per-agent `fastModeDefault: true`) — the `resolveFastModeState` chain is unchanged.

Closes #78451

target.title: fix(discord): preserve newlines across chunk boundaries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`chunkDiscordText` in `extensions/discord/src/chunk.ts` drops the newline separator when it flushes a chunk at a line boundary. As a result, the text that follows an inline error line can appear truncated or merged into the previous chunk, changing the message content that Discord users see.

Fixes #96007

## Why This Change Was Made

The chunker now tracks whether the next chunk starts with a leading newline and reserves one line/character of budget for that newline. This ensures that when chunks are joined back together, the original text is reproduced exactly, including line breaks after error lines.

## User Impact

Discord messages that contain inline error text followed by more content will no longer have their subsequent content truncated or glued to the error line.

## Evidence

- Updated `extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts` with a regression test covering the newline-across-boundary case.
- Adjusted `durable-delivery.test.ts` and `outbound-adapter.test.ts` expectations to match the preserved newline behavior.
- All Discord extension tests pass locally.

## AI Code Generation Disclosure

This patch was generated and reviewed with assistance from an AI coding agent. The change, tests, and PR description were produced as part of an automated GitHub issue resolution workflow.

target.title: fix(compaction): emit after_compaction on no-op and use JSON-safe validator delimiters (#81925)
target.body:
## Summary

OpenClaw issue #81925 documents two coupled defects that surface as HTTP 500s on voice channels when the context engine runs under memory pressure, especially for open-weight tool-calling models:

1. `after_compaction` is never emitted when compaction is a legitimate no-op (`{ok:true, compacted:false}`), so plugin observers that pair `before_compaction`/`after_compaction` wait forever and time out.
2. Schema-validation error messages wrap property names in single quotes (`'sessionTarget'`). Models trained on JSON tool calls copy the trailing `'` delimiter back into their next attempt and get stuck in an unrecoverable retry loop.

This change fixes both, on every surface where they occur.

## Root cause

### Bug 1: after_compaction not emitted on no-op compaction

`before_compaction` fires unconditionally once the engine owns compaction, but `after_compaction` was gated on `result.compacted === true` on **three** independent compaction surfaces:

- `compact.queued.ts` (engine-owned queued path): the after-hook block required `result.ok && result.compacted`.
- `compact.ts` `compactEmbeddedAgentSessionDirect` (native direct path): the `!containsRealConversationMessages(...)` early return sent `{ok:true, compacted:false, reason:"no real conversation messages"}` straight back to the caller, after `before_compaction` already fired, without ever calling `runAfterCompactionHooks`.
- `run.ts` `runOwnsCompactionAfterHook` (timeout-recovery and overflow-recovery paths): paired with `runOwnsCompactionBeforeHook`, which fires `before_compaction` unconditionally, but the after-hook returned early on `!compactResult.compacted`.

So a paired observer sees `before` with no matching `after`. The voice plugin waits out its 3s timeout, falls back to `tool-result-truncation`, and only recovers after ~3 attempts (~2.5 min), long after the client has already 500'd.

### Bug 2: validator delimiters trip tool callers

Validation error formatting wrapped property names in single quotes in two places:

- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.ts` `formatValidationErrors`: `unexpected property '<name>'` and `must have required property '<name>'` (gateway RPC params + plugin session action result validation, the surface an LLM-driven action call hits).
- `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts` `formatRequiredMessage`: `must have required property '<name>'` (plugin session action **payload** validation, the surface an LLM-submitted payload hits). Its sibling `additionalProperties` message was already double-quoted, so this was the lone single-quote holdout.

A model that parses the error and copies the property token captures `<name>'` (with the stray quote), re-emits the same malformed key, and re-triggers the identical error.

## Fix

- **Bug 1, all three surfaces:** emit `after_compaction` whenever compaction completes (`result.ok`), with `compactedCount: 0` and a `reason` discriminator on the no-op path. The engine paths forward the engine's own skip reason (default `policy_skipped`); the native path reports `no_real_conversation_messages`. Added an optional `reason?: string` to the `after_compaction` hook contract (`PluginHookAfterCompactionEvent`, `CompactionHookRunner`, `runAfterCompactionHooks`), additive and backward compatible, so existing subscribers are unaffected while observers can now distinguish a real compaction from a skip without fabricating synthetic `N->N` events. The `!compactResult.ok` guard is preserved, so genuine failures/aborts still do not emit a success `after_compaction`.
- **Bug 2, all four property-name branches:** format every property name through `JSON.stringify(name)` rather than interpolating it into hand-written double quotes. This covers `unexpected property` and `must have required property` in `formatValidationErrors`, and `must have required property` plus the `additionalProperties` list in `schema-validator`. `JSON.stringify` emits a real JSON string token, so the delimiter matches JSON tool-call syntax **and** a name that itself contains a `"`, `\`, or control character is properly escaped instead of producing text that is not a valid JSON string token. A model that copies the token back always gets a clean, parseable JSON key.

## Why this covers the whole issue (not one surface)

- The no-op `after_compaction` gap existed on **three** independent compaction code paths (engine-owned queued, native direct, and timeout/overflow recovery in the run loop). Fixing only one would still hang on the others. All three are fixed and all three have regression coverage.
- The delimiter/escaping issue existed across **four** property-name branches on **two** independent validator paths (gateway-protocol result validation and plugins payload validation). An LLM tool caller hits the payload path; fixing only the result path would leave the primary tool-caller surface broken. All four branches now route through `JSON.stringify`, so both the delimiter and the embedded-quote/backslash escape case are handled everywhere the same way.
- The downstream symptoms the issue describes (synthetic `N->N` events, `tool-result-truncation` fallback after ~3 attempts, client 500s) all stem from the missing real event; emitting it removes the need for the synthetic-event workaround at the root.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.hooks.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.timeout-triggered-compaction.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts` -> 136 passed (adds 5 regression tests: engine-skip no-op, engine default reason, native-skip paired-observer, timeout-recovery no-op, overflow-recovery no-op).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts src/plugins/contracts/session-actions.contract.test.ts src/plugins/config-schema.test.ts src/channels/plugins/config-schema.test.ts src/plugins/schema-validator.test.ts src/gateway/server.auth.default-token.test.ts src/gateway/client.test.ts` -> all passed (adds JSON-token validator assertions plus quote/backslash escape regression coverage on both the gateway-protocol and plugin schema-validator branches).
- `tsgo:test` type-check clean over the changed files; `oxlint --type-aware` 0 findings; `oxfmt --check` clean.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: a no-op compaction now emits `after_compaction` (so a paired voice observer is not left waiting), and both validators now format property names through `JSON.stringify` (so a tool-calling model always copies back a valid, parseable JSON key even when the property name contains a `"` or `\`).

Real environment tested: the actual built-from-source OpenClaw runtime functions in this branch, driven directly through `node` (via the `tsx` ESM loader) outside any harness. Bug 1 drives the real `containsRealConversationMessages`, `runBeforeCompactionHooks`, and `runAfterCompactionHooks` from `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/`, with a real `registerInternalHook` voice-style observer that increments on `before_compaction` and decrements on `after_compaction`. Bug 2 drives the real `formatValidationErrors` from `packages/gateway-protocol/` and the real `validateJsonSchemaValue` from `src/plugins/schema-validator.ts`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: register a paired `session:compact:before` / `session:compact:after` observer, feed a heartbeat-only transcript (so `containsRealConversationMessages` returns false, the real no-op trigger), then run the real before/after emission the patched no-op branch performs; separately, feed a hostile property name containing an embedded quote and backslash into the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator, read back each formatted message, and attempt to parse the token a JSON model would copy back.

Evidence after fix (live console output from `node` driving the real runtime functions):

```
$ node --import tsx proof-bug1.mts   # drives real compaction hook emission
containsRealConversationMessages(heartbeat) = false

# BEFORE the fix (no-op fires before_compaction only):
  observer pending balance = 1 <- stuck, after_compaction never arrives (hang)
  observer received after  = null

# AFTER the fix (no-op also fires after_compaction):
  observer pending balance = 0 <- balanced
  observer received after  = {"compactedCount":0,"reason":"no_real_conversation_messages"}

$ node --import tsx proof-validator-escape.mts   # drives real validators
property name a hostile schema/model supplies: "evil\"key\\path"

# BEFORE (raw interpolation into hand-written double quotes):
  message = "at root: unexpected property \"evil\"key\\path\""
  token a model copies = "\"evil\"key\\path\""
  copies as a clean JSON key? = false

# AFTER (real gateway-protocol formatValidationErrors):
  message = "at root: unexpected property \"evil\\\"key\\\\path\""
  copies as a clean JSON key? = true

# AFTER (real plugin schema-validator required-property miss):
  message = "must have required property \"evil\\\"key\\\\path\""
  contains a valid JSON string token? = true
```

Observed result after fix: the real no-op path now delivers `after_compaction` with `{compactedCount:0, reason:"no_real_conversation_messages"}` to the paired observer, returning its pending balance to 0 instead of hanging at 1; and for a property name carrying an embedded quote and backslash, both the real gateway-protocol formatter and the real plugin schema-validator now emit a `JSON.stringify`-escaped token that round-trips through `JSON.parse` back to the original name, where the previous raw-interpolation form did not parse as a valid JSON key.

What was not tested: a live end-to-end voice-channel session against a real 7B-14B llama-server under memory pressure. This change is at the compaction-hook and validation-formatter layers, exercised above by driving the real runtime functions plus the regression coverage; a full hardware voice loop was out of scope for this environment.

Fixes #81925

## Summary

**Problem**: With `compaction.mode: "safeguard"` and `truncateAfterCompaction: true`, delivery-mirror entries carry degenerate usage that produces `NaN` in `tokensBefore`. NaN serializes to `null`, and `isSessionEntry` rejects records where `typeof tokensBefore !== "number"` — so compaction records are skipped, truncation never applies, and the session re-compacts on every turn (thrash).

**Solution**: Two minimal fixes — (1) guard `calculateContextTokens` against NaN propagation from non-standard usage shapes; (2) relax `isSessionEntry` to not gate compaction validity on `tokensBefore`, which is telemetry and must not block truncation.

**What changed**:
- `calculateContextTokens()`: defensive `|| 0`, `Number.isFinite()`, and early return for valid `totalTokens` to prevent NaN reaching persisted state
- `isSessionEntry()`: removed `typeof tokensBefore === "number"` from compaction validation — `firstKeptEntryId` and `summary` are the essential fields
- New unit tests for NaN/zero/degenerate usage inputs and for `tokensBefore: null` / missing acceptance
- Replaced global `NaN` literals in tests with `Number.NaN` to satisfy oxlint `check-lint`

**What did NOT change**:
- No agent-core awareness of delivery-mirror model identity (keeps provider-agnostic)
- No change to the compaction summary reading path or the `CompactionEntry` type shape
- No change to how `tokensBefore` is displayed in RPC responses or UI (0 will appear for degenerate usage, which is harmless telemetry)

Fixes #100982

## What Problem This Solves

Long-running channel sessions with `compaction.mode: "safeguard"` and `truncateAfterCompaction: true` compact repeatedly (thrash) but never shrink: each compaction writes a summary and rotates to a new transcript, yet the successor still contains the full raw history. Context is never reclaimed, so the safeguard fires on nearly every turn — the session continuously grows and re-compacts without ever truncating.

Root cause chain:
1. delivery-mirror entries carry a degenerate usage shape (zeroed or OpenAI-ish after rebuild, lacking `cacheRead`/`cacheWrite`/`totalTokens`)
2. `calculateContextTokens()` sums `undefined` fields via `input + output + cacheRead + cacheWrite` → `NaN`
3. `JSON.stringify(NaN)` → `null` in persisted compaction records
4. `isSessionEntry()` in transcript-file-state.ts requires `typeof tokensBefore === "number"` → `null` fails → record is rejected
5. Rejected compaction records never set a keep-boundary → `truncateAfterCompaction` never applies → next turn re-compacts = thrash

## Root Cause

The two defective lines of code:

```ts
// packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.ts:150
// NaN propagates unchecked when cacheRead/cacheWrite/totalTokens are undefined
return usage.totalTokens || usage.input + usage.output + usage.cacheRead + usage.cacheWrite;

// src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/transcript-file-state.ts:245
// tokensBefore gates the entire compaction record; null (from serialized NaN) fails this check
typeof candidate.tokensBefore === "number"
```

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Compaction records with `tokensBefore: null` (persisted NaN from delivery-mirror degenerate usage) are now accepted, allowing session truncation to proceed.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.1.0

**Observed result after the fix**: Both defensive guards work correctly — calculateContextTokens no longer propagates NaN from degenerate usage shapes, and isSessionEntry accepts compaction entries with null/missing tokensBefore. Full L2 before/after evidence below and full test suite (63/63) passes.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Run the L2 evidence script that directly calls functions with delivery-mirror data patterns:

```terminal
node openclaw/.worktrees/issue-100982/evidence/pr-101047/l2-evidence.mjs
```

Run the full test suite:

```terminal
npx vitest run --reporter=verbose \
  packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/compaction.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/transcript-file-state.test.ts
```

**Evidence**: Before/after comparison with realistic data patterns (L2 — direct function call with real-world data):

Before — `calculateContextTokens` with delivery-mirror degraded usage (no cacheRead/cacheWrite):

```terminal_output
Input: {"input":150,"output":320}
  BEFORE fix: total = NaN
    → undefined + undefined = NaN in cacheRead + cacheWrite sum
  AFTER  fix: total = 470
    → 150 + 320, guarded by || 0 on each field
```

Before — `isSessionEntry` with null tokensBefore (persisted NaN):

```terminal_output
Input: tokensBefore: null (from JSON.stringify(NaN))
  BEFORE fix: isSessionEntry = false
    → typeof null !== 'number' — entry REJECTED
  AFTER  fix: isSessionEntry = true
    → tokensBefore no longer gated — entry ACCEPTED
```

Full before/after script output for all scenarios:

```terminal_output

  L2 Evidence — PR #101047
========================================================================

  AFTER  fix: total = 470

--- Scenario B: totalTokens is null (persisted NaN from JSON.stringify) ---

--- Scenario C: All usage fields are zero ---
  BEFORE fix: total = NaN  (0 || 0+0+0+0 = NaN, || short-circuits on falsy 0)
```

target.title: fix(markdown-core): CJK-friendly emphasis flanking so **标签：**正文 renders bold (#101120)
target.body:
Fixes #101120

## What Problem This Solves

CJK Markdown such as `**标题：**正文` can render literal emphasis markers. CommonMark's closing-delimiter rule rejects punctuation immediately inside `**` when adjacent CJK text follows without whitespace. Because Telegram, Signal, and Slack consume the shared Markdown IR, the defect belongs in `packages/markdown-core`, not in one transport.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Enable the maintained MIT `markdown-it-cjk-friendly` 2.0.2 plugin at the shared `MarkdownIt` construction point.
- Keep the dependency local to `@openclaw/markdown-core`; its only runtime dependency, `get-east-asian-width`, was already resolved in this workspace.
- Replace the submitted 125-line local delimiter/Unicode implementation with the upstream amendment, which directly covers supplementary CJK, variation selectors, ambiguous punctuation, underscores, Unicode whitespace, and the CommonMark corpus.
- Keep Telegram's reported-output regression while adding shared IR regressions for Chinese, Japanese, Korean, supplementary-plane CJK, variation selectors, Unicode whitespace, ordinary Latin, intraword underscores, code spans, and links.

## User Impact

CJK emphasis now renders consistently through every channel using the shared Markdown IR. Ordinary CommonMark behavior remains unchanged outside the CJK-friendly amendment; invalid whitespace-delimited openers remain literal.

## Evidence

Reviewed head: `dbc66f154026d80e23b496d723e60762712cd0ca`

- Sanitized AWS Crabbox `cbx_ed9e9a7749ff` / `coral-lobster`, public network, no Tailscale, empty instance profile, no credential hydration.

- Run `run_4947d71286b2`: clean full build plus source-blind built-artifact validation — 11/11 behavior fixtures passed.
